energy_risk_2012___kyos_power_plant_hedg.topic: Power plant delta hedging strategies and delta calculation methods

concepts.name: Delta sensitivity
concepts.scope: The change in power plant value with respect to a small change in a forward commodity price, used to quantify hedging exposure per traded product period.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between the power price and the cost of gas plus carbon required to generate one unit of electricity, determining plant dispatch profitability.

concepts.name: Dark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between the power price and the cost of coal plus carbon required to generate electricity from a coal-fired plant.

concepts.name: Spark spread option
concepts.scope: A financial option whose payoff equals the spark spread when positive and zero otherwise, capturing the optionality inherent in power plant dispatch.

concepts.name: Margrabe's formula
concepts.scope: A closed-form spread option pricing model that values the right to exchange one asset for another, applied here to value power plants as spread options on power versus fuel-plus-carbon.

concepts.name: Intrinsic value
concepts.scope: The plant value calculated from current forward price levels only, treating the plant as fully dispatched or idle with no recognition of price uncertainty or hourly flexibility.

concepts.name: Hourly intrinsic value
concepts.scope: An extension of intrinsic value that shapes the forward curve to hourly granularity but still ignores forward price variability and optionality.

concepts.name: Cointegration
concepts.scope: A long-run equilibrium relationship between commodity prices (e.g. power and fuel) that constrains spark spread dynamics and is absent from the standard Margrabe framework.

concepts.name: Gradual linear hedging strategy
concepts.scope: A benchmark approach that sells equal expected production volumes along the forward curve over the hedging horizon, balancing price and liquidity risk.

concepts.name: Hedging benchmark
concepts.scope: The target forward sale volume defined as a fraction of expected future production, against which actual trading positions are monitored.

concepts.name: Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM)
concepts.scope: The price process assumed by Margrabe's formula for the combined fuel-plus-carbon leg of the spread, implying log-normally distributed prices.

concepts.name: Take-or-pay constraint
concepts.scope: A contractual obligation requiring a plant operator to pay for a minimum fuel volume regardless of actual dispatch, creating inflexibility in hedging and dispatch.

concepts.name: Oil-indexed gas contract
concepts.scope: A long-term gas supply contract whose price is linked to oil indices rather than gas market quotes, creating additional commodity exposure for plant operators.

concepts.name: Asset-backed trading
concepts.scope: Trading activity directly linked to and constrained by physical plant positions, distinguished from speculative positions for risk attribution and capital allocation purposes.

concepts.name: Power purchasing agreement (PPA)
concepts.scope: A structured long-term contract for the forward sale of power output, used as an alternative or supplement to exchange-traded hedging instruments.

methods: Monte Carlo simulation of forward and spot prices
Dynamic programming for optimal plant dispatch
Delta calculation by average simulated production per period
Delta calculation by finite-difference price shocking
Volatility and correlation term structure estimation

likron_powerplants.topic: Optimised power plant hedging in futures markets using dynamic clean spread strategies

concepts.name: Clean spread
concepts.scope: The margin derived by subtracting fuel and emission rights costs from the electricity price, used as the core hedging underlying for thermal plant profitability.

concepts.name: Static hedge
concepts.scope: A fixed futures position that does not adjust to changing spread levels or plant operation schedules over time.

concepts.name: Dynamic hedging
concepts.scope: Continuous adjustment of futures positions in response to spread movements to maximise expected profit within a prescribed risk budget.

concepts.name: Hourly resolved operation schedule
concepts.scope: A time-granular plan of plant dispatch identifying which individual hours are profitable given current spread levels and technical constraints.

concepts.name: Hedge size
concepts.scope: The quantity of futures contracts held, calibrated to match the expected profitable operating hours of the plant.

concepts.name: Risk budget
concepts.scope: A prescribed limit on financial risk exposure within which hedge adjustments must remain.

concepts.name: Bid-offer spread
concepts.scope: The transaction cost arising from low liquidity in energy markets that increases the cost of rebalancing futures positions.

concepts.name: Calendar base/peak futures
concepts.scope: Standardised futures contracts covering base-load or peak-load delivery over a calendar period used as hedging instruments for generation capacity.

concepts.name: Plant technical flexibility
concepts.scope: The operational constraints of a power plant that bound the feasible set of hourly dispatch decisions during schedule optimisation.

concepts.name: Back testing
concepts.scope: Validation of hedging strategies against both historical market data and simulated price scenarios to assess performance and robustness.

implied_prerequisites: Power plant economics and dispatch logic

pareto_spikes.topic: Non-Markovian power price spike modeling and European contingent claim valuation

concepts.name: Non-Markovian power price process
concepts.scope: A power spot price model defined as the product of a spike process and an inter-spike process, yielding a process that requires extended state information beyond the current price.

concepts.name: Two-state Markov chain (spike/inter-spike)
concepts.scope: A continuous-time two-state Markov process whose states determine whether the power market is currently in a spike or a regular inter-spike regime.

concepts.name: Spike process
concepts.scope: A Markov process equal to a random multiplicative magnitude during spikes and unity between spikes, constructed from the two-state Markov chain and a spike-magnitude distribution.

concepts.name: Inter-spike process
concepts.scope: A Markov diffusion process modeling power prices between spikes, typically specified as a geometric mean-reverting process.

concepts.name: Geometric mean-reverting process
concepts.scope: A diffusion model for inter-spike power prices featuring drift toward a time-varying equilibrium level with stochastic volatility, used as the baseline price dynamics between spikes.

concepts.name: Pareto distribution for spike magnitude
concepts.scope: A heavy-tailed probability distribution on (1, ∞) used to characterise the multiplicative size of power price spikes, parameterised by a shape and minimum-magnitude parameter.

concepts.name: Transition probability decomposition
concepts.scope: A splitting of spike-state transition probabilities into a component for remaining continuously in the spike state and a component for re-entering it after an inter-spike period.

concepts.name: Kolmogorov-Chapman equation
concepts.scope: A semigroup consistency condition for Markov transition matrices, used here to derive analytical expressions for the two-state transition matrix and its generator.

concepts.name: Generator matrix
concepts.scope: A 2×2 matrix characterising the instantaneous rate of change of the two-state Markov transition matrix, with off-diagonal entries controlling spike frequency and duration.

concepts.name: Ergodic probabilities
concepts.scope: Long-run stationary probabilities for the spike and inter-spike states of the two-state Markov chain, governing the limiting behaviour of forward prices and option values.

concepts.name: European contingent claim on power with spikes
concepts.scope: A claim whose payoff may depend on the power price, the current spike/inter-spike state, and the spike magnitude at expiry, valued as a discounted risk-neutral expectation.

concepts.name: Risk-neutral average payoff over spike magnitude
concepts.scope: The conditional expectation of the state-dependent payoff over the spike-magnitude distribution, reducing a spiking-market valuation to a no-spike contingent claim problem.

concepts.name: Eigenclaim method
concepts.scope: An analytical technique representing contingent claim payoffs as power functions of the underlying price, enabling closed-form valuation in both Black-Scholes and mean-reverting environments.

concepts.name: Asymmetric power option
concepts.scope: A European option whose payoff is a power of the underlying asset price, allowing analytical valuation in both Black-Scholes and mean-reverting settings via moment-generating properties.

concepts.name: Power forward price with spikes
concepts.scope: The risk-neutral expected future spot price of power accounting for spikes, expressed as the no-spike forward price multiplied by a risk-neutral average spike magnitude.

concepts.name: Characteristic spike lifetime
concepts.scope: A small dimensionless parameter equal to the ratio of mean spike duration to mean inter-spike interval, used to derive first-order spike corrections to option values.

concepts.name: Option value spike-smoothing property
concepts.scope: The result that European option values on power do not exhibit spikes when time to expiry is large relative to mean spike duration, because state-dependent values converge exponentially fast.

concepts.name: Forward price spike-smoothing property
concepts.scope: The analogous result that power forward prices for distant maturities are insensitive to whether the spot is currently in a spike, differing only by exponentially small corrections.

concepts.name: Product integral
concepts.scope: A generalisation of the matrix exponential used when Markov generators do not commute at different times, arising in time-inhomogeneous two-state spike models.

concepts.name: Put-call parity for spiking power markets
concepts.scope: Parity relationships between call and put values that hold in both the mean-reverting and Black-Scholes environments, extended to asymmetric power and Pareto-averaged payoffs.

concepts.name: Ergodic average spike magnitude
concepts.scope: The long-run stationary expected multiplicative spike factor used to scale inter-spike forward prices when time-to-maturity is large relative to spike lifetime.

concepts.name: Power forward price with spikes (delivery period)
concepts.scope: The risk-neutral forward price for electricity delivered over an interval [T1,T2] expressed as the ergodic spike magnitude times the inter-spike forward price up to exponentially small corrections.

concepts.name: Short-lived spike approximation
concepts.scope: A perturbative expansion of forward prices and contingent claim values in powers of the characteristic spike-occupation time tch when spike lifetime is much shorter than inter-spike waiting time.

concepts.name: European contingent claim on power forwards with spikes
concepts.scope: A derivative whose value equals a Black-Scholes-type value evaluated at a rescaled payoff and forward price, with corrections of order exp(-a(T-t)).

concepts.name: Ergodic implied volatility
concepts.scope: The Black-Scholes implied volatility of options on power forwards with spikes, obtained by inverting ergodic-regime call or put pricing formulas.

concepts.name: Pareto-distributed spike magnitude
concepts.scope: A heavy-tailed distribution for the multiplicative spike size with tail index gamma, leading to modified call/put pricing formulas with finite-moment restrictions gamma > omega_n.

concepts.name: Delta hedging of power contingent claims
concepts.scope: Standard Black-Scholes delta hedging applied to European claims on power forwards when time-to-maturity is large relative to expected spike lifetime.

concepts.name: Put-call parity for spiked power options
concepts.scope: The preservation of standard put-call parity relationships for approximate call and put prices on forwards on power with spikes in both ergodic and short-lived spike regimes.

concepts.name: Vega of power contingent claims
concepts.scope: The Black-Scholes vega formula used to linearize the implied volatility correction due to spikes in the short-lived spike perturbative expansion.

concepts.name: Geometric mean-reverting inter-spike price
concepts.scope: The risk-neutral dynamics of electricity prices outside spike periods, governed by a mean-reverting lognormal process with time-dependent drift.

concepts.name: Spike characteristic time (tch)
concepts.scope: The product of spike probability and expected spike lifetime, used as the small expansion parameter in the short-lived spike perturbation series.

plant_hedging_and_trading_strategies_kyo.topic: Power plant hedging and delta calculation strategies

concepts.name: Delta hedging
concepts.scope: The strategy of trading forward contracts in quantities equal to the expected production (delta) of a power plant to reduce price exposure.

concepts.name: Delta sensitivity
concepts.scope: The partial derivative of plant value with respect to a forward price, used to determine the correct hedge volume per commodity and period.

concepts.name: Dark spread
concepts.scope: The profit margin of a coal-fired power station, defined as the difference between the power price and the coal cost of generation.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The profit margin of a gas-fired power station, defined as power price minus fuel cost minus carbon cost adjusted for plant efficiency.

concepts.name: Spark spread option
concepts.scope: The optionality of a gas-fired plant to run only when the spark spread is positive, valued as a call option on the spread.

concepts.name: Intrinsic value approach
concepts.scope: A static dispatch method that treats the plant as fully in-the-money or fully out-of-the-money based solely on current forward spread levels, ignoring price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Real option value
concepts.scope: The additional expected profit arising from the plant's flexibility to dispatch only when profitable, above the intrinsic forward margin.

concepts.name: Margrabe's formula
concepts.scope: A closed-form spread option pricing model that treats each leg of the spread as a geometric Brownian motion to derive option value and delta sensitivities.

concepts.name: Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM)
concepts.scope: A continuous-time stochastic process with log-normally distributed returns, used as the price dynamics assumption in Black-Scholes-type models.

concepts.name: Cointegration
concepts.scope: A long-run equilibrium relationship between power and fuel prices that keeps spark spreads within a narrow bandwidth and is ignored by Margrabe's formula.

concepts.name: Gradual linear hedging strategy
concepts.scope: A benchmark strategy that builds up forward hedge volumes uniformly over the hedging horizon until expected production is fully covered before delivery.

concepts.name: Risk premium
concepts.scope: The discount producers may accept when selling power forward relative to expected spot realisation, arising from asymmetric hedging demand between producers and consumers.

concepts.name: Expected production (hedge volume)
concepts.scope: The probability-weighted average output of the plant used as the target forward sale quantity to minimise profit variance.

concepts.name: Power purchasing agreement (PPA)
concepts.scope: A structured long-term contract for the sale of power output, used as an alternative to liquid forward market hedging.

concepts.name: Take-or-pay contract
concepts.scope: A structured gas supply contract imposing minimum offtake obligations that affect the effective marginal fuel cost and dispatch decision.

concepts.name: Oil-indexed gas contract
concepts.scope: A gas supply agreement where the price is linked to oil rather than a gas market hub, creating additional commodity cross-exposures for the plant.

concepts.name: Hourly dispatch flexibility
concepts.scope: The plant's ability to vary output on an hourly basis, which determines the realistic delta profile and is not captured by monthly spread option models.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo simulation for plant valuation
concepts.scope: A full simulation approach that generates many price scenarios and optimises dispatch in each to compute expected production and delta sensitivities accurately.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming for dispatch optimisation
concepts.scope: An optimisation technique used to find the plant's optimal dispatch schedule subject to physical constraints across simulated price paths.

concepts.name: Value-at-Risk (VaR)
concepts.scope: A risk metric quantifying potential portfolio losses at a given confidence level, used in capital allocation and trading book oversight.

concepts.name: Forward curve shaping
concepts.scope: The decomposition of monthly or quarterly forward prices into hourly granularity to capture intraday price structure in valuation.

concepts.name: Asset-backed trading
concepts.scope: Trading activity directly linked to physical plant positions and hedging benchmarks, kept separate from speculative positions for accurate profit attribution.

Delta calculation by price shocking and revaluation
Delta calculation by average simulated production

Carbon market basics (EU ETS, CO2 pricing)

powerhedging.topic: Power plant delta-hedging strategies and delta calculation methods

concepts.name: Delta sensitivity
concepts.scope: The change in power plant value with respect to a small change in a forward commodity price, used to determine hedge volumes.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between the power price and the cost of gas and carbon required to produce one unit of power at a given efficiency.

concepts.name: Dark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between the power price and the cost of coal and carbon required to produce one unit of power.

concepts.name: Spark spread option
concepts.scope: A call option on the spark spread representing the plant owner's right to dispatch only when the spread is positive.

concepts.name: Margrabe's formula
concepts.scope: A closed-form spread-option pricing model used to value power plants and compute delta hedges by treating the plant as an exchange option on two commodities.

concepts.name: Intrinsic value approach
concepts.scope: A static valuation method that dispatches the plant based solely on current forward spread levels, ignoring price uncertainty and hourly optionality.

concepts.name: Hourly intrinsic value
concepts.scope: A refined intrinsic approach that shapes the forward curve to hourly granularity before computing plant value, still ignoring price variability.

concepts.name: Cointegration
concepts.scope: A long-run equilibrium relationship between commodity prices that constrains spark spread dynamics and is absent from standard GBM-based spread option models.

concepts.name: Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM)
concepts.scope: The continuous-time price process assumed for commodity prices in Margrabe's formula, characterised by constant drift and volatility.

concepts.name: Gradual linear hedging strategy
concepts.scope: A benchmark approach that builds hedge volume incrementally over the hedging horizon by selling equal forward volumes on average across time.

concepts.name: Hedging benchmark
concepts.scope: A target hedge volume schedule defined as a product of a gradual time-based ramp and expected future production, against which actual hedge positions are monitored.

concepts.name: Asset-backed trading
concepts.scope: Trading activity directly linked to and bounded by the physical asset position, kept separate from speculative proprietary positions for performance attribution.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming dispatch model
concepts.scope: An optimisation technique used to determine the economically optimal dispatch schedule for a power plant subject to its physical operating constraints.

concepts.name: Plant dispatch constraints
concepts.scope: Physical operating restrictions on a power station such as start costs, minimum run-times, heat delivery obligations, and take-or-pay commitments.

concepts.name: Volatility term structure
concepts.scope: The schedule of forward price return volatilities across delivery periods used as input to spread option models.

concepts.name: Correlation term structure
concepts.scope: The schedule of return correlations between commodity forward prices across delivery periods used in multi-commodity hedging models.

concepts.name: Oil-indexed gas contracts
concepts.scope: Long-term gas supply agreements where the gas price is linked to oil price indices rather than traded gas market quotes.

concepts.name: Power purchasing agreement (PPA)
concepts.scope: A structured long-term contract for the sale of power output from a plant, used as an alternative to exchange-traded forward hedging.

concepts.name: Take-or-pay contract
concepts.scope: A fuel supply contract obligating the buyer to pay for a minimum volume regardless of actual consumption, creating a floor on fuel cost exposure.

concepts.name: Value-at-risk (VaR)
concepts.scope: A statistical measure of the potential loss on a portfolio over a given horizon and confidence level, used for capital allocation and risk reporting.

concepts.name: Plant dispatch
concepts.scope: The decision to generate at full capacity or zero based on whether the market spread exceeds the variable cost threshold.

concepts.name: Clean spark spread (CSS)
concepts.scope: The net margin from generating power after accounting for fuel and carbon costs, used as the effective price signal for dispatch.

concepts.name: Optionality value of a generation asset
concepts.scope: The additional value captured by dispatching conditionally on each simulated price path rather than at a fixed average volume.

concepts.name: Average dispatch fallacy
concepts.scope: The error of computing plant value by multiplying average dispatch volume by average price, which systematically understates expected value.

concepts.name: Stochastic price simulation
concepts.scope: Monte Carlo simulation of forward price paths used to value generation assets and origination deals under uncertainty.

concepts.name: Delta hedging
concepts.scope: Hedging strategy based on the sensitivity of expected asset value to a parallel shift in simulated forward prices.

concepts.name: Delta (generation asset)
concepts.scope: The change in expected dispatch value per unit change in the forward spread, computed by bumping simulated prices and revaluing.

concepts.name: Variable cost
concepts.scope: The per-MWh cost of generation that sets the strike level determining whether the plant runs on each simulated path.

concepts.name: Bump-and-revalue
concepts.scope: Numerical method for estimating delta by shifting all simulated prices by a small increment and comparing the resulting expected values.

concepts.name: Expected value under simulation
concepts.scope: The arithmetic mean of path-wise revenues computed after applying the optimal dispatch decision on each simulated price path.

concepts.name: N(d1) as contingent stock-receipt factor
concepts.scope: N(d1) is the factor by which the present value of receiving the stock contingent on exercise exceeds the current stock price.

concepts.name: Risk-adjusted (risk-neutral) probabilities
concepts.scope: A probability measure obtained by replacing the drift parameter µ with the riskless rate r, under which discounted asset prices are martingales.

concepts.name: Contingent exercise payment
concepts.scope: The component of the call payoff representing payment of the exercise price only if the option finishes in the money.

concepts.name: Contingent stock receipt
concepts.scope: The component of the call payoff representing delivery of the stock only if the option finishes in the money.

concepts.name: Truncated lognormal expectation
concepts.scope: The expected value of a lognormal random variable conditioned on exceeding a threshold, used to value the contingent stock-receipt component.

concepts.name: Lognormal stock price distribution
concepts.scope: The assumption that log(S_T) is normally distributed with drift and variance parameters µ and σ² under the physical measure.

concepts.name: One-period binomial option pricing
concepts.scope: A single-step discrete model where the call value is expressed as a discounted risk-neutral expectation with analogues of N(d1) and N(d2).

concepts.name: Multi-period binomial option pricing
concepts.scope: An n-step binomial model whose call pricing formula involves complementary binomial distribution functions that correspond to N(d1) and N(d2).

concepts.name: Complementary binomial distribution function
concepts.scope: The probability that a binomial random variable equals or exceeds a threshold a, used as the discrete analogue of the Black-Scholes normal probability terms.

concepts.name: Hedge ratio (delta)
concepts.scope: The number of shares needed to replicate the option, equal to N(d1) in Black-Scholes but not equal to the analogous factor in the binomial model.

concepts.name: Continuously compounded rate of return
concepts.scope: The logarithmic return log(S_t/S)/t, which is normally distributed with mean µ − σ²/2 and variance σ²/t under the physical measure.

concepts.name: Risk-neutral drift substitution
concepts.scope: The probability adjustment that replaces µ with r in the lognormal distribution to obtain the risk-neutral pricing measure.

methods: Decomposition of call payoff into two contingent claims
Truncated lognormal expectation formula with proof
Standardisation of lognormal variable to derive d1 and d2
Multi-period binomial formula restatement using complementary binomial distribution
implied_prerequisites: Discounted expected value / present value calculations
Basic stochastic processes for asset prices

the_caveats_in_aom_peak_delta_calculatio.topic: AOM Peak Delta Calculation Methodology and Caveats

concepts.name: Baseload Delta
concepts.scope: The full average baseload delta of a CCGT asset as produced directly by AOM optimisation output.

concepts.name: Incremental Peak Delta
concepts.scope: The marginal delta attributable to peak hours, derived by decomposing the full baseload delta using scalar sensitivity runs in AOM.

concepts.name: Composite Baseload Delta
concepts.scope: The residual baseload delta remaining after subtracting the incremental peak delta from the full CCGT delta, used for hedging off-peak exposure.

concepts.name: Peak Scalar
concepts.scope: A scalar applied to peak-hour prices within AOM to shift peak price levels for sensitivity calculations without altering overall price.

concepts.name: Scalar Sensitivity Run
concepts.scope: An AOM run in which peak scalars are shifted by a small increment and off-peak scalars adjusted inversely, used to isolate peak price sensitivity.

concepts.name: Station Value Change
concepts.scope: The difference in optimised station value between the scalar sensitivity run and the base run, used as the numerator in delta calculations.

concepts.name: Peak Price Change
concepts.scope: The correctly computed change in peak price, defined as the change in peak scalar multiplied by the baseload price rather than the peak price.

concepts.name: 7-Day Peak vs 5-Day Peak
concepts.scope: The distinction between AOM's monthly-granularity optimisation covering all seven days and market-traded peak forward contracts covering only the five working days.

concepts.name: EFA Blocks
concepts.scope: UK electricity market settlement periods (EFA blocks 3, 4, and 5) that define peak hours within AOM's optimisation framework.

concepts.name: Delta Decomposition
concepts.scope: The process of splitting a CCGT's full delta into mutually exclusive peak and baseload components for front-office hedging purposes.

concepts.name: AOM (Asset Optimisation Model)
concepts.scope: An in-house optimisation model operating at monthly granularity that produces station values and baseload deltas but does not distinguish weekday from weekend.

concepts.name: ISM Line
concepts.scope: An internal benchmark based on dispatch volumes from optimisation output, used as the basis for trading decisions and transfer pricing.

concepts.name: Transfer Pricing between Desks
concepts.scope: The internal financial settlement between Power Generation and Midstream desks based on incremental peak and composite baseload delta figures.

methods: Two-run AOM comparison (base run vs scalar sensitivity run)
Delta decomposition via finite difference approximation
Adjustment scaling of 7-day to 5-day peak delta

UK electricity market structure and EFA periods
Asset optimisation modelling for thermal generation
Price scalar construction in optimisation models

concepts.name: Fundamental (Stack) Model
concepts.scope: A market-level dispatch model that minimises total generation costs to produce price and generation forecasts.

concepts.name: Optimisation Model
concepts.scope: A plant-level model that maximises asset operating value given exogenous price inputs and plant operating constraints.

concepts.name: Short-Run Marginal Cost (SRMC)
concepts.scope: The variable cost of producing one additional unit of electricity, used to order plant in the merit stack.

concepts.name: Merit Order / Supply Stack
concepts.scope: The ranking of generation units by marginal cost to determine dispatch sequence and market clearing price.

concepts.name: Marginal Cost Pricing
concepts.scope: The principle that the market clearing price equals the SRMC of the last unit dispatched to meet demand.

concepts.name: Asset Valuation
concepts.scope: The process of estimating the operating value of a power plant or tolling agreement using dispatch optimisation.

concepts.name: Tolling Agreement
concepts.scope: A contractual arrangement valued by the optimisation model that grants rights to dispatch a plant against given fuel and power prices.

concepts.name: Plant Operating Constraints
concepts.scope: Technical limits on a generation unit including start-up costs and ramp-up/ramp-down rates that bound feasible dispatch.

concepts.name: Interconnector Availability
concepts.scope: A capacity constraint representing cross-border transmission limits included in fundamental dispatch models.

concepts.name: NPV Approach
concepts.scope: A discounted cash-flow valuation method noted as a limitation of fundamental models for not capturing optionality.

concepts.name: Carbon Cost
concepts.scope: The cost of CO2 emissions allowances included as a fuel-related input in both fundamental and optimisation models.

concepts.name: Power Demand Forecast
concepts.scope: A projected load profile used as the key demand-side input to fundamental dispatch models.

implied_prerequisites: Familiarity with fuel and carbon markets

concepts.name: Peak Delta
concepts.scope: The price differential between peak and off-peak power products expressed as an incremental scalar or spread.

concepts.name: Baseload Price
concepts.scope: The flat around-the-clock reference price used as the foundation for deriving peak and off-peak valuations.

concepts.name: Peak Price
concepts.scope: The price applicable to on-peak delivery hours, derived by applying a scalar to the baseload price.

concepts.name: Off-Peak Price
concepts.scope: The price applicable to off-peak delivery hours, implied residually from baseload and peak prices given their volumetric weights.

concepts.name: Peak Scalar
concepts.scope: A multiplicative factor applied to the baseload price to obtain the peak price, capturing the ratio of peak to flat value.

concepts.name: Around-the-Clock (ATC) Averaging
concepts.scope: The volumetric weighting of peak and off-peak hours to reconcile component prices back to the baseload flat price.

concepts.name: Shape Value
concepts.scope: The incremental value attributable to the hourly load shape relative to a flat baseload position.

methods: Scalar multiplication of baseload price to derive peak price
Volumetric hour-weighting (e.g. 10 MWh off-peak, 15 MWh peak) to back out implied off-peak price
Algebraic decomposition of around-the-clock price into peak and off-peak components
Delta calculation as difference between peak and baseload price levels

Hour-count conventions for peak and off-peak periods

concepts.name: Peak scalar (PK scalar)
concepts.scope: A weighting factor that allocates a contract's exposure between peak and off-peak periods.

concepts.name: Delta (AV / delta-V)
concepts.scope: First-order price sensitivity of a position's value to a small shift in market price.

concepts.name: Incremental shift (0.01 shift)
concepts.scope: A standardised one-cent or one-unit bump applied to isolate marginal price sensitivity.

concepts.name: BI (block instrument / base instrument notional)
concepts.scope: The notional quantity or block size of the instrument used to scale delta calculations.

concepts.name: SPK (super-peak or shaped-peak quantity)
concepts.scope: The portion of the block instrument quantity attributable to peak-shaped exposure.

concepts.name: OBI (off-peak block instrument component)
concepts.scope: The residual block instrument quantity after removing the peak-shaped component.

concepts.name: Price scalar
concepts.scope: A multiplier converting a raw price shift into a market-price-equivalent delta in MWh terms.

concepts.name: CEBL (contract or exposure base level)
concepts.scope: A base-level contract exposure term combined with scaled peak contributions to form total delta.

concepts.name: Delta decomposition
concepts.scope: Separation of total value sensitivity into peak and off-peak components using scalar weighting.

concepts.name: SAK term
concepts.scope: An additive adjustment factor applied alongside the CEBL to compute the full incremental delta.

methods: Linear delta decomposition by peak/off-peak allocation
Algebraic rearrangement of block-instrument delta into peak and residual components

pk_op_to_incrpk_and_comb_bl.topic: Peak, Off-Peak, and Incremental Peak Power Product Decomposition

concepts.name: Peak (Pk) product
concepts.scope: A power delivery product covering on-peak hours within a scheduling period.

concepts.name: Off-Peak (OP) product
concepts.scope: A power delivery product covering off-peak hours within a scheduling period.

concepts.name: Incremental Peak (IncPk) product
concepts.scope: A product representing the incremental or differential quantity between two peak-related positions.

concepts.name: Base (Base) product
concepts.scope: A flat around-the-clock power delivery product covering all hours in a scheduling period.

concepts.name: Product decomposition identity
concepts.scope: The arithmetic relationship expressing how peak, off-peak, and incremental peak quantities combine to replicate a base-load position.

concepts.name: Delta (delta) position
concepts.scope: The net incremental exposure arising from combining or stripping standard power products.

concepts.name: CCGT intrinsic value
concepts.scope: Value of a combined-cycle gas turbine expressed as a weighted sum of spark-spread call options across operating levels.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between power price and gas cost (adjusted by heat rate) that determines CCGT dispatch profitability.

concepts.name: Heat rate
concepts.scope: The ratio of fuel input to electrical output used to convert gas prices into power-equivalent cost at different load levels.

concepts.name: SEL and MEL
concepts.scope: Stable Export Limit and Maximum Export Limit defining the minimum and maximum generation output levels of the plant.

concepts.name: Replication by time-of-use segment
concepts.scope: Decomposition of plant cash flows into weekday peak, weekday off-peak, weekend daytime and weekend night-time buckets for separate calibration.

concepts.name: Piecewise call-option regression
concepts.scope: Fitting multiple call-option terms with distinct volume, heat-rate and strike parameters to replicate non-linear dispatch cash flows.

concepts.name: R-squared goodness of fit
concepts.scope: Proportion of variance in modelled cash flows explained by the replicating portfolio across each time-of-use segment.

concepts.name: Explained value (hour-weighted)
concepts.scope: Aggregate replication accuracy measured as the percentage of total plant value captured by the portfolio, weighted by settlement hours.

methods: Piecewise linear regression with call-option basis functions
Ordinary least squares calibration of replication parameters

rough_results.topic: Unit root testing of UK electricity forward/baseload price ratios

concepts.name: Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test
concepts.scope: Tests whether a time series has a unit root (non-stationarity) against the alternative of stationarity.

concepts.name: Stationarity
concepts.scope: Property of a time series whose statistical moments do not change over time, required for many econometric models.

concepts.name: EFA (Electricity Forward Agreement) price
concepts.scope: Standardised UK electricity forward contract price used as the time series under analysis.

concepts.name: Baseload price
concepts.scope: Flat around-the-clock electricity price used here as a denominator to form a spread or ratio.

concepts.name: Peak/baseload ratio
concepts.scope: Ratio of peak-period forward prices to baseload prices, tested for stationarity as a potential cointegrating relationship.

concepts.name: Cointegration via ratio stationarity
concepts.scope: Empirical approach that checks whether a price ratio is stationary as a proxy for a long-run equilibrium between two price series.

concepts.name: Lag order selection in ADF
concepts.scope: Choice of the number of lagged difference terms included in the ADF regression to correct for serial correlation.

concepts.name: Weekend/weekday seasonality segmentation
concepts.scope: Splitting electricity price data into weekend and weekday sub-samples to account for systematic intra-week demand patterns.

concepts.name: p-value truncation warning
concepts.scope: Numerical artefact where the reported p-value is floored at 0.01 when the true p-value is smaller, relevant when interpreting ADF results.

Basic hypothesis testing and p-value interpretation

risksimulationstudy.topic: Clean Spark Spread simulation and extreme price impact analysis

concepts.name: Clean Spark Spread (CSS)
concepts.scope: The net margin from generating electricity with gas after accounting for fuel and carbon costs.

concepts.name: Extreme price events in Monte Carlo simulation
concepts.scope: Occurrence of very high or low simulated commodity prices that lie far outside the typical distribution range.

concepts.name: Price correlation across commodity legs
concepts.scope: The degree to which power, gas, and carbon prices move together within a simulation, affecting spread volatility.

concepts.name: Percentile-based risk metrics (P5/P95)
concepts.scope: Statistical quantiles used to characterise the lower and upper tails of a simulated price or value distribution.

concepts.name: Impact of outlier iterations on average valuation
concepts.scope: How a single extreme simulation path can shift the mean CSS estimate, scaled by the total number of iterations.

concepts.scope: The dependence of valuation accuracy on the time period modelled, with extreme tail events accumulating over longer horizons.

concepts.name: Forward curve shaping
concepts.scope: Deriving granular forward price curves from liquid traded products using historical ratio-based shaping across month-quarter, quarter-season, and workday-weekend dimensions.

concepts.name: Product ratio method
concepts.scope: Estimating intra-period price shape by averaging historical ratios between overlapping or nested contract prices.

concepts.name: No-arbitrage curve construction
concepts.scope: Ensuring that shaped forward curves are consistent with observable market prices so no risk-free profit can be extracted across overlapping contracts.

concepts.name: Overlapping contract handling
concepts.scope: Resolving conflicts or redundancies when multiple traded contracts cover the same delivery period within a forward curve.

concepts.name: Local volatility
concepts.scope: Point-in-time instantaneous volatility of an energy price process calibrated to market data for a specific tenor.

concepts.name: Terminal volatility
concepts.scope: Integrated volatility of an energy price process over the full time horizon to expiry, used for option pricing.

concepts.name: Correlation surface
concepts.scope: Estimated co-movement structure between energy commodities—peak power, off-peak power, gas, and carbon—used as input to spread option pricing.

concepts.name: Generation cost (GenCost) volatility
concepts.scope: Direct statistical estimation of the volatility of the variable cost of generation, combining fuel and carbon price dynamics.

concepts.name: Kirk approximation
concepts.scope: Closed-form analytical approximation for pricing spread options on two or more underlyings, applied here as a three-legged variant for power tolling payoffs.

concepts.name: Spark spread / clean spark spread (CSS) option
concepts.scope: Option on the spread between power price and generation cost (fuel plus carbon), representing the optionality in a power tolling agreement.

concepts.name: Strip of daily options
concepts.scope: Decomposition of a tolling agreement into a sequence of daily peak and off-peak spread options covering the entire deal period.

concepts.name: Intrinsic versus extrinsic value split
concepts.scope: Decomposition of a tolling option's total value into the deterministic in-the-money component and the time-value component arising from price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Greeks / Delta
concepts.scope: Price sensitivities of the tolling valuation to movements in underlying forward prices and volatilities, used for hedging.

concepts.name: Peak / off-peak power price distinction
concepts.scope: Separation of power forward curves and volatilities into on-peak and off-peak delivery periods reflecting intraday demand patterns.

concepts.name: Adaptive pricer calling
concepts.scope: Computational efficiency technique that reduces option pricer invocations by grouping homogeneous days or using iterative refinement where value changes slowly.

concepts.name: Backtesting engine
concepts.scope: Framework for retrospectively evaluating valuation model performance against historical market outcomes.

concepts.name: Object-oriented (OO) valuation wrapper
concepts.scope: Software design pattern encapsulating deal inputs, pricing logic, and output for a strip of energy options within a reusable class structure.

methods: Historical ratio averaging for forward curve shaping
Monte Carlo simulation (referenced for benchmark testing)

concepts.name: Forward Curve Shaping
concepts.scope: The process of disaggregating longer-tenor contract prices (seasonal, quarterly, annual) into shorter-tenor prices (monthly, daily) using historical ratio relationships.

concepts.name: Contract Breakdown Hierarchy
concepts.scope: The structured mapping of larger period contracts (e.g. Winter season) into their smaller constituent contracts (e.g. Q1, Q2) for cascading price decomposition.

concepts.name: Historical Price Ratios
concepts.scope: The average ratio of a shorter-tenor contract price to its parent longer-tenor contract price, estimated over a lookback window of traded days.

concepts.name: Normalised Monthly Ratios
concepts.scope: Ratio adjustments applied to ensure that the weighted average of disaggregated shorter-period prices is consistent with the parent contract price.

concepts.name: Last Trading Day Effects
concepts.scope: The distortion in price ratios near contract expiry, mitigated by excluding a buffer of trading days before the last trading day from the historical sample.

concepts.name: Weekend/Weekday Price Ratio
concepts.scope: The empirical ratio of weekend (WEND) to day-ahead (DA) prices by calendar month, used to split monthly average prices into weekday and weekend daily prices.

concepts.name: Daily Shaping
concepts.scope: The application of weekend/weekday ratios to monthly average prices to produce distinct weekday and weekend price estimates for each day in the curve.

concepts.name: Off-Peak Power Price
concepts.scope: The implied price for off-peak power hours, derived algebraically from baseload and peak power prices.

concepts.name: Value Date
concepts.scope: The reference date for which the forward curve is constructed, determining which snapshot of market prices is extracted from the historical data file.

concepts.name: Overlapping Contract Discarding
concepts.scope: The rule whereby, when granular and broader contracts cover the same period, the smaller explicitly quoted contracts take precedence and the implied breakdown of the larger contract is discarded.

concepts.name: Gregorian vs EFA Calendar
concepts.scope: The distinction between the standard Gregorian calendar assumed for power contracts in this implementation and the Electricity Forward Agreement calendar conventionally used in GB power markets.

concepts.name: Bid-Offer Mid Price
concepts.scope: The arithmetic mid-point between bid and offer quotes used as the representative price for ratio and curve calculations.

concepts.name: Off-Peak Price Derivation
concepts.scope: Computing off-peak power prices as a residual from baseload and peak power prices using load-weighted arithmetic.

concepts.name: Last Trading Day Identification
concepts.scope: Determining the final traded date for each contract to define the boundary of usable historical price data.

concepts.name: End-of-Trading-Period Exclusion
concepts.scope: Removing a buffer of trading days prior to contract expiry from the lookback sample to avoid price distortion near expiry.

concepts.name: Value Date
concepts.scope: The specific date for which the forward curve is extracted from historical data and subsequently shaped.

concepts.name: Overlapping Contract Resolution
concepts.scope: The rule by which shorter-tenor contracts are discarded in favour of longer-tenor contracts when both cover the same delivery period.

concepts.name: EFA Calendar

concepts.scope: The arithmetic mid-point between bid and offer quotes used as a single representative price for a contract.

humbertollvaluation.topic: Tolling Agreement Valuation (CSS Options on UK Power/Gas Spread)

concepts.name: Tolling Agreement
concepts.scope: A contractual structure giving the holder the right to convert gas into power at a physical plant for a variable cost (toll fee), modelled as a strip of spark-spread options.

concepts.name: Commodity Spread Swap (CSS) Option
concepts.scope: A daily option on the spread between UK power and NBP gas prices, with physical delivery, forming the building block of the tolling strip.

concepts.name: Intrinsic Value
concepts.scope: The value of the tolling strip based solely on current forward prices without accounting for future price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Unshaped Intrinsic Value
concepts.scope: Intrinsic value computed using only seasonal (quarterly/seasonal) forward price granularity before any intra-period shaping is applied.

concepts.name: Shape Value
concepts.scope: Incremental value gained by moving from seasonal to monthly forward curves using market-derived month/quarter, season/quarter, and weekday/weekend ratio shapes.

concepts.name: Extrinsic (Time) Value
concepts.scope: The component of option value attributable to volatility and correlation of the underlying commodities beyond what is captured in current forward prices.

concepts.name: Local Volatility Term Structure
concepts.scope: The modelled relationship between implied volatility and time-to-maturity for each commodity, capturing the stylised fact that near-dated contracts are more volatile than far-dated ones.

concepts.name: Correlation Term Structure
concepts.scope: The modelled relationship between pairwise commodity correlations (power peak, off-peak, gas, carbon) and time-to-maturity, capturing increasing correlation at longer tenors.

concepts.name: Peak/Off-Peak/Baseload Decomposition
concepts.scope: Splitting the tolling option strip into separate weekday peak, weekday off-peak, and weekend baseload option components for valuation and risk purposes.

concepts.name: Delta
concepts.scope: First-order sensitivity of the tolling value to changes in the underlying base, peak, or off-peak forward power prices, computed on a monthly bucket basis.

concepts.name: Capacity Fee
concepts.scope: A fixed monthly payment per MW made by the buyer to the seller under the tolling agreement, benchmarked against the calculated extrinsic value per unit of capacity.

concepts.name: BSUoS and NTS Charges
concepts.scope: Balancing Services Use of System and National Transmission System SO Exit charges modelled as additional variable costs borne by the buyer within the tolling structure.

concepts.name: Clean Spark Spread (CSS) Option

concepts.name: Intrinsic Value (Shaped)

concepts.scope: The time-value component of the option strip reflecting volatility and correlation of power, gas, and carbon beyond the shaped forward curve.

concepts.name: Correlation Term Structure

0067_short_term_generation_asset_valuati.topic: Short-term power plant valuation under physical operating constraints using stochastic optimisation

concepts.name: Generation asset valuation
concepts.scope: Determination of the expected profit value of a power plant over a short operating horizon under price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The difference between the electricity price and the product of the heat rate and fuel price, representing per-unit operating margin.

concepts.name: Spark spread call option
concepts.scope: A financial option whose payoff equals the positive part of the spark spread, used in the financial-options approach to plant valuation.

concepts.name: Multi-stage stochastic optimisation
concepts.scope: A sequential decision framework in which commitment choices are made before prices are revealed at each hourly stage.

concepts.name: Unit commitment
concepts.scope: The binary on/off scheduling decision for a generation unit, subject to minimum uptime, downtime, and lead-time constraints.

concepts.name: Minimum uptime constraint
concepts.scope: The requirement that once a unit is started it must remain online for at least a specified number of periods.

concepts.name: Minimum downtime constraint
concepts.scope: The requirement that once a unit is shut down it must remain offline for at least a specified number of periods.

concepts.name: Startup cost
concepts.scope: The fuel and labour cost incurred when bringing an offline unit back online, modelled as a function of boiler cooling time.

concepts.name: Commitment lead time
concepts.scope: The advance notice period required before a unit can become operational, capturing boiler heat-up dynamics.

concepts.name: Heat rate
concepts.scope: The thermal input per unit of electrical output of a generator, used to convert fuel cost into electricity production cost.

concepts.name: Input-output characteristic
concepts.scope: A quadratic function relating total fuel consumption (MMBtu/h) to generator output level (MW).

concepts.name: State variable
concepts.scope: An integer recording how long a unit has been continuously online or offline, encoding the relevant operational history for constraint checking.

concepts.name: Indifference locus
concepts.scope: A curve in electricity–fuel price space at which the expected value of turning the unit on equals the expected value of turning it off.

concepts.name: Cost-to-go function
concepts.scope: The optimal expected profit from a given state at time t to the end of the operating horizon, computed by backward dynamic programming.

concepts.name: Mean-reverting price process
concepts.scope: An Itô process for log-prices in which prices are pulled back toward a seasonal long-run mean at a rate proportional to displacement.

concepts.name: Lognormal price distribution
concepts.scope: The distributional assumption for electricity and fuel prices implied by modelling log-prices as a mean-reverting Gaussian diffusion.

concepts.name: Value at Risk (VaR)
concepts.scope: The loss threshold at a specified confidence level over the operating period, derived from the simulated profit distribution.

concepts.name: Maximum likelihood estimation
concepts.scope: Calibration of mean-reversion speed, long-run mean, and volatility parameters of the price processes from historical price data.

concepts.name: Downside risk
concepts.scope: The probability and magnitude of negative profits arising from physical operating constraints that prevent the operator from responding optimally to adverse prices.

methods: Maximum likelihood estimation of Itô process parameters

concepts.name: Load-price relationship

concepts.name: Forced outage modelling
concepts.scope: Representing time-to-failure and time-to-repair as exponential distributions to capture random unplanned plant unavailability.

concepts.name: Path-dependent dispatch algorithm
concepts.scope: A simulation-based dispatch logic that conditions current operating decisions on prior-period states to respect operational constraints.

concepts.name: Generator state machine
concepts.scope: A discrete set of mutually exclusive operational states (e.g., maximum generation, ramping, forced outage) with permissible transitions governing plant dispatch.

concepts.name: Minimum up and down time constraints
concepts.scope: Requirements that a plant remain online or offline for at least a specified number of hours before changing status.

concepts.name: Ramp rate constraints
concepts.scope: Physical limits on the rate at which a generator can increase or decrease output, varying by hot, warm, and cold start conditions.

concepts.name: Heat-rate curve
concepts.scope: A function expressing fuel input per unit of electricity output as a function of generation level, reflecting efficiency variation across the dispatch range.

concepts.name: Start-up costs

concepts.name: Spark-spread cashflow
concepts.scope: The net revenue per period from operating a gas-fired unit, computed as generation times the difference between power price and heat-rate-adjusted fuel cost.

concepts.scope: A forward-looking heuristic that compares projected cashflows over minimum commitment periods against start-up costs to decide whether to commit the unit.

concepts.name: Earnings-at-risk (EaR)

concepts.name: Expanded forward curve

concepts.name: Emission costs

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between power revenue and fuel cost for a gas-fired generator, used as the primary value driver for dispatch decisions.

concepts.name: Intrinsic value
concepts.scope: The plant value derived from locking in current forward spark spreads, ignoring price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Extrinsic value
concepts.scope: The additional value above intrinsic value arising from price volatility and operational flexibility, also called real option value.

concepts.name: Real option value
concepts.scope: The economic value embedded in the operational flexibility of a physical asset to respond to future price movements.

concepts.name: Perfect foresight assumption
concepts.scope: The modelling simplification that treats future price paths as fully known when making dispatch decisions, leading to overstatement of plant value.

concepts.name: Non-perfect foresight
concepts.scope: A modelling framework in which dispatch decisions are made using only currently observable price information rather than future realised prices.

concepts.name: Least-squares Monte Carlo (LSMC)
concepts.scope: A simulation-based method that uses cross-sectional regressions of simulated payoffs on state variables to estimate continuation values at each decision node.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming (backward valuation)
concepts.scope: A recursive optimisation technique that solves for optimal decisions by working backwards from the terminal period through all states and time steps.

concepts.name: State space
concepts.scope: The set of all variables the optimiser must track simultaneously, including current operational status, hours online/offline, and cumulative starts.

concepts.name: Short-history constraint
concepts.scope: An operational constraint determined by recent plant history, such as minimum run-time or minimum down-time requirements.

concepts.name: Long-history constraint
concepts.scope: An operational constraint that depends on accumulated actions over a longer horizon, such as an annual cap on the number of starts.

concepts.name: Shadow cost
concepts.scope: An iteratively adjusted implicit penalty applied to starts to enforce a hard start-count limit within a dynamic programming framework without expanding the state space.

concepts.name: Minimum run-time / minimum down-time
concepts.scope: Operational constraints requiring the plant to remain online or offline for a minimum number of hours after each state transition.

concepts.name: Start cost
concepts.scope: An explicit or implicit cost incurred each time the plant is restarted, covering fuel consumption and wear, which may vary by cold, warm, or hot start type.

concepts.name: Cold/warm/hot start classification
concepts.scope: A categorisation of restart costs based on the duration the unit has been offline, reflecting the thermal state of the plant.

concepts.name: Hard start-count limit
concepts.scope: A contractual or engineering constraint capping the total number of plant starts permitted within a defined period, common in VPP contracts.

concepts.name: Virtual Power Plant (VPP) contract
concepts.scope: A contractual arrangement granting a counterparty dispatch rights over a physical plant, often including explicit start-number limitations.

concepts.name: Continuation value
concepts.scope: The expected present value of future cash flows from holding an asset in its current state, used to compare against immediate-action payoffs in dynamic programming.

concepts.name: Cointegration (power and fuel prices)
concepts.scope: A statistical relationship linking power prices to fuel costs through merit-order fundamentals, keeping spark spreads mean-reverting within plausible bounds.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo price simulation
concepts.scope: A stochastic simulation method generating many possible future price paths for power and fuel, capturing volatility and dependence structures.

concepts.name: Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP)
concepts.scope: An alternative deterministic optimisation approach that formulates dispatch as a set of linear constraints and binary on/off variables.

concepts.name: Minimum stable generation
concepts.scope: The lowest output level at which a thermal plant can operate continuously without shutting down, associated with a lower efficiency than full load.

concepts.name: Dispatch optimisation
concepts.scope: The process of determining the optimal hourly production schedule for a plant to maximise profit subject to technical and contractual constraints.

concepts.name: Regression basis functions (LSMC)
concepts.scope: The set of observable price variables, such as current spark spread and recent average spread, used as regressors to estimate continuation values in LSMC.

deng_real_options_approach.topic: Real options valuation of electricity tolling agreements

concepts.name: Tolling agreement
concepts.scope: A supply contract granting the buyer the right to take output from a generation asset by paying a predetermined premium, subject to operational and contractual constraints.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between the electricity price and the heat-rate-adjusted fuel cost, representing the instantaneous payoff of operating a thermal generator.

concepts.name: Heat rate
concepts.scope: A measure of generator fuel efficiency expressed as units of fuel (MMBtu) consumed per unit of electricity (MWh) produced, varying with output level.

concepts.name: Operational option
concepts.scope: The right but not obligation of a plant operator to generate electricity, whose payoff at each time step equals the positive spark spread.

concepts.name: Real option
concepts.scope: A managerial flexibility right on a physical asset valued using financial option-pricing theory, here applied to the decision to start or stop electricity generation.

concepts.name: Restart constraint
concepts.scope: A contractual limit on the maximum number of plant restarts permitted over the tolling contract's life, reducing operational flexibility and contract value.

concepts.name: Ramp-up delay
concepts.scope: The time period required for a generating unit to reach minimum output after starting from the off state, during which fuel costs are incurred but no electricity is produced.

concepts.name: Startup and shutdown costs
concepts.scope: Fixed costs borne by the tolling contract holder whenever the plant transitions from off to on or from on to off.

concepts.name: Stochastic dynamic programming (SDP)
concepts.scope: A backward-induction optimisation framework that determines the value function of the tolling contract by maximising expected discounted payoffs over all admissible operating actions.

concepts.name: Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equations
concepts.scope: The recursive optimality conditions characterising the value function of the tolling contract across all plant operational states and price scenarios.

concepts.name: Value function approximation
concepts.scope: Approximation of the conditional expected continuation value in the dynamic programme by a truncated polynomial basis expansion whose coefficients are fitted by least-squares regression.

concepts.name: Least-squares Monte Carlo (LSM)
concepts.scope: A simulation-based method that estimates continuation values in American-style option problems by regressing realised future values onto basis functions of current state variables.

concepts.name: Mean-reverting process (Ornstein–Uhlenbeck)
concepts.scope: A continuous-time diffusion model for log-commodity prices that pulls the process back toward a long-run mean at a speed proportional to the current deviation.

concepts.name: Mean-reverting jump-diffusion process
concepts.scope: An extension of the mean-reverting diffusion model that superimposes a compound Poisson jump component to capture the spikes observed in electricity prices.

concepts.name: Correlated commodity price processes
concepts.scope: Joint modelling of electricity and natural gas log-prices as bivariate stochastic processes with a specified instantaneous correlation coefficient.

concepts.name: On-peak / off-peak price scaling
concepts.scope: A discretisation device that multiplies simulated daily prices by different scaling factors for peak and off-peak hours to reflect the intra-day price pattern in power markets.

concepts.name: No-arbitrage pricing
concepts.scope: The principle that the discount rate in the SDP equals the risk-free rate when operating payoffs can be perfectly replicated by traded forward contracts on electricity and fuel.

concepts.name: Incomplete market risk premium
concepts.scope: An additional spread added to the risk-free discount rate when traded instruments cannot perfectly hedge the real option payoff, reflecting unhedgeable market risk.

concepts.name: Price regime and stationarity
concepts.scope: The assumption that the parameters of the commodity price processes remain constant over the contract horizon, with non-stationarity leading to systematic mis-valuation.

concepts.name: Euler discretisation of SDEs
concepts.scope: A numerical scheme that approximates continuous-time stochastic differential equations by first-order finite-difference updates used to simulate price paths.

concepts.name: Tolling agreement
concepts.scope: A temporary lease contract granting an agent operational control and dispatch rights over an energy asset such as a gas-fired power plant.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between the electricity price and the cost of the gas required to produce it, representing the instantaneous profitability of running a generation unit.

concepts.name: Heat rate
concepts.scope: The fuel-to-power conversion ratio of a generation unit, quantifying how many MMBtu of gas are needed to produce one MWh of electricity.

concepts.name: Optimal switching
concepts.scope: A stochastic control problem in which an agent selects the timing and direction of regime changes to maximise total expected reward net of switching costs over a finite horizon.

concepts.name: Stochastic impulse control
concepts.scope: A continuous-time control framework in which the controller applies a sequence of discrete interventions, each incurring a cost, to a stochastically evolving state process.

concepts.name: Recursive optimal stopping
concepts.scope: A reformulation of impulse or switching control as a nested sequence of single optimal stopping problems solved iteratively by induction on the number of remaining switches.

concepts.name: Snell envelope
concepts.scope: The smallest càdlàg supermartingale dominating a reward process, characterising the value function of an optimal stopping problem and identifying the optimal stopping time.

concepts.name: Value function
concepts.scope: The maximal conditional expected reward achievable from a given state, time, and operating regime under the optimal switching policy.

concepts.name: Intervention operator
concepts.scope: An operator mapping current state and number of remaining switches to the best value obtainable by making an immediate regime change, net of switching costs.

concepts.name: Switching boundary
concepts.scope: A free boundary in state-time space separating the continuation region (no switch optimal) from the exercise region (immediate switch optimal), analogous to the exercise boundary of an American option.

concepts.name: Quasi-variational inequality (QVI)
concepts.scope: A system of partial differential inequalities characterising the value function of an impulse or switching control problem, comprising a PDE in the continuation region and an obstacle condition in the exercise region.

concepts.name: Reflected backward stochastic differential equation (RBSDE)
concepts.scope: A BSDE augmented with a constraint that keeps the solution above a time-varying barrier, with a compensator process ensuring the solution touches the barrier as infrequently as possible.

concepts.name: Viscosity solution
concepts.scope: A generalised notion of solution to a PDE or QVI that ensures existence and uniqueness without requiring classical differentiability, used here to characterise the switching value function.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming principle
concepts.scope: The Bellman optimality property stating that the value function at any intermediate time equals the supremum over controls of the cumulative reward to that time plus the continuation value function.

concepts.name: Hysteresis band
concepts.scope: The range of state values in which the operator neither switches on nor off because switching costs make the change sub-optimal, leading to investment inertia.

concepts.name: Operational delay and time separation
concepts.scope: Constraints on the switching control requiring a minimum time interval between successive regime changes, modelling physical ramp-up and ramp-down requirements of power plants.

concepts.name: Exponential Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
concepts.scope: A mean-reverting log-normal diffusion used to model commodity prices, ensuring positivity while capturing the empirical stationarity observed in energy spreads.

concepts.name: Sub-additive switching costs
concepts.scope: A triangle-inequality condition on transition costs that makes direct switches between any two regimes always at least as cheap as routing through an intermediate regime.

concepts.name: Bermudan approximation
concepts.scope: The restriction of switching times to a discrete time grid, approximating the continuous-time American switching right and introducing a discretisation error of order sqrt(Δt).

concepts.name: Longstaff-Schwartz (LS) regression scheme
concepts.scope: A least-squares Monte Carlo algorithm that updates optimal stopping times pathwise using regressed continuation values, avoiding direct storage of regressed quantities to reduce bias.

concepts.name: Tsitsiklis-van Roy (TvR) regression scheme
concepts.scope: A Monte Carlo dynamic programming algorithm that directly replaces conditional expectations with their regression approximations at each time step, yielding a tractable but potentially biased estimator.

concepts.name: Basis function projection
concepts.scope: The approximation of conditional expectation operators by projection onto a finite-dimensional function space spanned by chosen basis functions such as polynomials or exponentials.

concepts.name: Discretisation error
concepts.scope: The approximation error introduced by applying the Euler scheme to the state SDE and restricting exercise to a discrete time grid, bounded in Lp norm at order sqrt(Δt).

concepts.name: Projection error
concepts.scope: The error arising from replacing the true conditional expectation with its projection onto a finite basis, which accumulates across time steps and magnifies across switching layers.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo sampling error
concepts.scope: The statistical error from using a finite number of simulated paths to estimate regression coefficients and value functions, expected to decay at rate O((Δt·N)^{-1/2}).

concepts.name: Gronwall's inequality (discrete)
concepts.scope: A discrete-time stability lemma bounding cumulative errors in backward recursions by exponential growth in the remaining time, used throughout the convergence analysis.

concepts.name: Real options
concepts.scope: The application of financial option theory to managerial flexibility in physical investment projects, including decisions to start, suspend, or abandon production under price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Longstaff-Schwartz least-squares regression
concepts.scope: Simulation-based backward-induction algorithm that approximates conditional expectations via cross-sectional regression on basis functions to value the continuation region.

concepts.name: Tsitsiklis-Van Roy regression
concepts.scope: Alternative Monte Carlo regression scheme for approximating value functions of American-style problems, noted for lower variance but higher bias than Longstaff-Schwartz.

concepts.name: Reflected BSDE
concepts.scope: Backward stochastic differential equation with a reflection constraint, providing a probabilistic representation of the value functions in the optimal switching framework.

concepts.name: Sampling error
concepts.scope: Error due to estimating regression coefficients from a finite number N of simulated Monte Carlo paths rather than the true distribution.

concepts.name: Empirical truncation
concepts.scope: Analytical device applied to regression estimates to enforce a priori bounds on simulated value function values and prevent error blow-up.

concepts.name: Quantization method
concepts.scope: Numerical scheme that approximates the continuous state process by an adaptive finite grid, pre-computing transition probabilities offline for use in dynamic programming.

concepts.name: Markov chain approximation
concepts.scope: Method of replacing continuous state dynamics with a finite-state continuous-time Markov chain on a rectangular grid to enable exact backward recursion.

concepts.name: Kernel regression
concepts.scope: Nonparametric conditional expectation estimator using k-nearest-neighbour weighted averages with a smooth kernel function in place of parametric basis functions.

concepts.name: Strip of spread options
concepts.scope: Practitioner approximation valuing a generation asset as a sum of European spark-spread options at each delivery period, ignoring switching costs and hysteresis.

concepts.name: Exhaustible resource management
concepts.scope: Extension of the optimal switching framework to mines or oilfields where cumulative production depletes a finite resource inventory over a finite licence horizon.

concepts.name: Outage modelling
concepts.scope: Incorporation of random forced shutdowns via memoryless exponential inter-arrival times that modify the reward integral and recursive value function structure.

concepts.name: Curse of dimensionality
concepts.scope: Exponential growth in grid size with state dimension that makes PDE and Markov chain methods computationally infeasible for problems with more than two or three state variables.

concepts.name: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
concepts.scope: Mean-reverting continuous diffusion used to model commodity prices such as power, gas and oil exhibiting stationary stochastic behaviour.

concepts.name: Operational delay
concepts.scope: Minimum time interval enforced between successive regime switches to reflect physical ramp-up or fuel-changeover constraints of a generation plant.

concepts.name: Gronwall inequality
concepts.scope: Analytical tool used in convergence proofs to bound accumulated errors in recursive backward schemes by controlling error propagation across time steps.
