the_value_of_starting_up_a_power_plant_w.topic: Power plant valuation with start-stop constraints using Least-Squares Monte Carlo

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between power revenue and gas fuel cost for a gas-fired plant, used as the primary value driver.

concepts.name: Intrinsic value
concepts.scope: Plant value computed from the deterministic forward spark spread curve assuming optimal dispatch.

concepts.name: Extrinsic (flexibility) value
concepts.scope: Additional value above intrinsic value arising from price uncertainty and the optionality to respond to realised spot prices.

concepts.name: Real options
concepts.scope: The framework treating plant operational flexibility (run, stop, start) as options whose value depends on future price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Perfect foresight assumption
concepts.scope: The modelling simplification that the operator knows all future prices when making dispatch decisions, which overstates plant value.

concepts.name: Non-perfect foresight
concepts.scope: The realistic condition where operators can only estimate future prices, reducing the achievable value from flexible assets.

concepts.name: Least-Squares Monte Carlo (LSMC)
concepts.scope: A simulation-based method that estimates continuation values via regression to optimise sequential decisions without perfect foresight.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming
concepts.scope: A backward-induction optimisation framework that finds the optimal dispatch policy by solving sub-problems across a state-space grid.

concepts.name: State-space representation
concepts.scope: The set of variables (online/offline duration, cumulative starts) the plant model must track to determine feasible actions and costs.

concepts.name: Short-history constraint
concepts.scope: Operational restrictions based on recent plant status such as minimum run-time or minimum down-time requirements.

concepts.name: Long-history constraint
concepts.scope: Restrictions that depend on cumulative plant behaviour over a longer period, such as a hard annual cap on the number of starts.

concepts.name: Shadow cost for starts
concepts.scope: An implicit penalty per start iteratively calibrated so that the optimal dispatch respects a maximum annual start limit.

concepts.name: Start cost (hot/warm/cold)
concepts.scope: Explicit costs incurred when restarting a plant that vary with how long the unit has been offline.

concepts.name: Minimum run-time
concepts.scope: A constraint requiring the plant to remain online for a minimum number of hours before it may be shut down.

concepts.name: Maximum annual starts constraint
concepts.scope: A hard upper bound on the number of times a plant may start within a year, common in Virtual Power Plant contracts.

concepts.name: Virtual Power Plant (VPP)
concepts.scope: A contractual arrangement that grants a counterparty rights over a plant's flexible capacity, typically including constraints on start frequency.

concepts.name: Cointegration of power and fuel prices
concepts.scope: A statistical relationship anchoring power prices to fuel fundamentals so that spark spreads remain within economically plausible bounds over time.

concepts.name: Continuation value
concepts.scope: The expected future value of holding a position or keeping a plant in a given state, used in backward dynamic programming and LSMC.

concepts.name: Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP)
concepts.scope: An alternative deterministic optimisation approach that formulates dispatch as a set of linear constraints with binary on/off variables.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo price simulation
concepts.scope: Stochastic generation of many possible price paths for power, gas, and carbon used to value plant flexibility in expectation.

concepts.name: Multi-commodity multi-factor forward curve model
concepts.scope: A price model that jointly captures movements in power, gas, and carbon forward curves using multiple stochastic factors.

concepts.name: Regime-switching spot price model
concepts.scope: A spot price model that allows abrupt changes between distinct price regimes to capture spikes and low-price periods.

concepts.name: Plant degradation cost
concepts.scope: An implicit cost reflecting reduced asset life or increased maintenance expenditure caused by frequent start-stop cycling.

concepts.name: Minimum stable generation level
concepts.scope: The lowest output at which a thermal plant can operate continuously, below which it must shut down.

methods: Least-Squares Monte Carlo (LSMC) with regression-based continuation value estimation
Backward dynamic programming with state-space enumeration
Shadow cost iteration for start-limit enforcement
Monte Carlo simulation with cointegrated multi-commodity price model
Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) for dispatch (discussed as benchmark)
Sensitivity analysis across start cost levels, minimum run-times, and annual start caps
implied_prerequisites: Power market fundamentals and merit order

worldpower2009_realisticpowerplantvaluat.topic: Power plant valuation using cointegrated energy price simulation

concepts.name: Intrinsic value
concepts.scope: The discounted value of a power plant computed from static forward spark-spread curves without any optionality.

concepts.name: Extrinsic / flexibility value
concepts.scope: The incremental value above intrinsic value arising from the ability to adapt dispatch decisions dynamically to realised price outcomes.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The gross margin per MWh of a gas-fired plant, equal to the power price minus fuel cost adjusted for plant heat rate, plus CO2 cost.

concepts.name: Dark spread
concepts.scope: The gross margin per MWh of a coal-fired plant, equal to the power price minus coal fuel cost adjusted for heat rate and CO2 cost.

concepts.name: Cointegration
concepts.scope: An econometric relationship capturing stable long-run price-level linkages between power, fuel and carbon prices, preventing unrealistic spread extremes in simulation.

concepts.name: Merit order
concepts.scope: The cost-ranked dispatch sequence of generation technologies that fundamentally anchors power prices to fuel and carbon costs.

concepts.name: Real options approach
concepts.scope: Treating a power plant as a portfolio of spark-spread call options to capture the value of operational flexibility under price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo price simulation
concepts.scope: Stochastic simulation of joint commodity price paths used to estimate the distribution of power plant cash flows and option values.

concepts.name: Correlated returns model
concepts.scope: A Monte Carlo approach using a correlation matrix of daily price returns that captures short-horizon co-movement but fails to bound long-horizon spread levels.

concepts.name: Multi-factor forward curve model
concepts.scope: A parameterised stochastic model capturing level shifts, contango-to-backwardation transitions and seasonal spread dynamics across the forward curve.

concepts.name: Regime-switching spot prices
concepts.scope: A price model component that generates infrequent large spikes in spot power or gas prices with mean reversion back to forward curve levels.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming dispatch optimisation
concepts.scope: A backward-induction algorithm that derives the optimal hourly start/stop and output decisions for a plant subject to technical and contractual constraints.

concepts.name: Minimum run-time and minimum off-time constraints
concepts.scope: Technical restrictions requiring a thermal plant to remain on or off for a minimum number of consecutive hours, reducing theoretical flexibility value.

concepts.name: Start costs
concepts.scope: Fixed fuel consumption and maintenance expenses incurred each time a thermal plant is started, penalising frequent cycling.

concepts.name: Variable O&M costs
concepts.scope: Operating and maintenance expenses that scale with production hours or number of starts, reducing net spark-spread margin.

concepts.name: Planned maintenance and plant trips
concepts.scope: Scheduled outage days and unplanned forced outages that reduce available generation capacity and thus plant value.

concepts.name: Plant degradation
concepts.scope: Gradual decline in thermal efficiency over time that increases fuel consumption per MWh and reduces plant value.

concepts.name: Take-or-pay gas contract
concepts.scope: A contractual minimum gas offtake obligation that constrains dispatch flexibility by imposing a minimum annual operating-hour requirement.

concepts.name: Static hedge
concepts.scope: A forward sale of the expected production volume and purchase of fuels and CO2 at the start of the evaluation period, held without subsequent adjustment.

concepts.name: Dynamic hedge
concepts.scope: A rolling hedge strategy that re-balances forward positions as expected production volumes change with evolving spark-spread levels, improving risk-return profile.

concepts.name: Delta hedge
concepts.scope: A hedge volume equal to the sensitivity of plant value to the underlying commodity price, approximated here by the volume-weighted expected production.

concepts.name: Net present value (NPV) analysis
concepts.scope: A static discounted cash flow method applied to power plant investment that ignores the value of operational flexibility.

concepts.name: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) in commodity simulation
concepts.scope: A dimensionality-reduction technique applied to the commodity return covariance matrix as an alternative to a full correlation matrix in Monte Carlo models.

concepts.name: Contango and backwardation
concepts.scope: Forward curve shapes where prices are respectively above or below current spot, relevant to calibrating multi-factor commodity models.

methods: Monte Carlo simulation of joint commodity price paths
implied_prerequisites: Forward curve construction for power, gas and carbon
Energy commodity markets (power, gas, coal, CO2)
Heat rate and efficiency concepts for thermal generation

worldpower2010_thevalueofstartingupthepo.topic: Gas-fired power plant valuation with start-stop constraints using Least-Squares Monte Carlo

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin between power price and fuel cost scaled by plant efficiency, used as the key profitability signal for dispatch decisions.

concepts.name: Intrinsic value
concepts.scope: Plant value computed from current forward spark spread curves assuming deterministic future prices.

concepts.name: Extrinsic (flexibility) value
concepts.scope: Additional value above intrinsic arising from price uncertainty and the optionality of flexible dispatch.

concepts.name: Real option value
concepts.scope: The economic worth embedded in the plant operator's ability to choose production hours in response to evolving market prices.

concepts.name: Strip of European call options
concepts.scope: A simplified plant valuation model treating each hour as an independent call option on the spark spread, ignoring inter-temporal constraints.

concepts.name: Start costs
concepts.scope: Explicit and implicit costs incurred each time a plant is restarted, including fuel consumption and wear-dependent maintenance penalties.

concepts.name: Hot/warm/cold start classification
concepts.scope: Temperature-dependent categorisation of restart costs based on the duration the unit has been offline.

concepts.name: Minimum run-time constraint
concepts.scope: An operational restriction requiring the plant to remain online for a minimum number of hours before being allowed to shut down.

concepts.name: Hard start-number limit
concepts.scope: A contractual or mechanical cap on the total number of starts permitted within a given period, common in VPP contracts.

concepts.name: Short-history state
concepts.scope: A dynamic-programming state variable tracking recent consecutive on/off hours to enforce minimum up/down time constraints.

concepts.name: Long-history state
concepts.scope: A dynamic-programming state variable accumulating total starts since period start to enforce annual start-count limits.

concepts.name: Shadow cost for starts
concepts.scope: An iteratively calibrated implicit penalty per start used to enforce a start-count limit within a standard dynamic programming framework.

concepts.name: Perfect foresight assumption
concepts.scope: The modelling simplification that the operator knows all future price realisations when making dispatch decisions, which overstates plant value.

concepts.name: Least-Squares Monte Carlo (LSMC)
concepts.scope: A simulation-based backward-induction method that uses cross-sectional regressions to estimate continuation values without assuming perfect price foresight.

concepts.name: Continuation value regression
concepts.scope: A polynomial regression of discounted future payoffs on current state variables used in LSMC to approximate the value of keeping the plant in a given state.

concepts.name: Cointegration of power and fuel prices
concepts.scope: A long-run equilibrium relationship linking electricity prices to fuel fundamentals that bounds spark spread behaviour in simulation models.

concepts.name: Multi-factor forward curve model
concepts.scope: A stochastic model with multiple risk factors driving movements in the forward price curve for power and fuel.

concepts.name: Regime-switching spot price model
concepts.scope: A spot price specification that allows the price process to switch between distinct statistical regimes to capture spikes and mean reversion.

concepts.name: Virtual Power Plant (VPP) contract
concepts.scope: A contractual arrangement granting a counterparty dispatch rights over a physical plant, often including explicit start-number restrictions.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming for plant dispatch
concepts.scope: A backward-induction optimisation that computes the value-maximising dispatch decision at each time-state node over the plant's operating horizon.

concepts.name: State-space expansion
concepts.scope: The increase in the number of model states when the long-history start-count variable is added as an extra dimension in dynamic programming.

concepts.name: Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP)
concepts.scope: An alternative dispatch optimisation formulation using binary commitment variables and linear constraints, noted for ignoring price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Minimum stable generation level
concepts.scope: The lowest output at which a CCGT plant can operate continuously, below which a full shutdown is required.

methods: Least-Squares Monte Carlo (Longstaff-Schwartz algorithm applied to energy assets)
Shadow-cost iterative calibration for start-count constraints
State-space dynamic programming with long-history start counter
Monte Carlo price simulation with cointegration and regime switching
Polynomial cross-sectional regression for continuation value estimation
Mixed-integer linear programming (benchmarked, not primary method)
implied_prerequisites: Forward curve modelling for power and gas
Spark spread mechanics and CCGT plant economics
Energy market structure and VPP contracts

deng_johnson_sogom_dss_2001.topic: Electricity derivatives pricing and real options valuation of generation and transmission assets

concepts.name: Spark spread option
concepts.scope: A derivative whose payoff depends on the difference between the electricity price and the product of a strike heat rate and fuel price.

concepts.name: Locational spread option
concepts.scope: A derivative whose payoff depends on the price difference of electricity between two geographical locations.

concepts.name: Heat rate
concepts.scope: A measure of generation efficiency defined as the units of fuel input required to produce one unit of electrical output.

concepts.name: Futures-based replication
concepts.scope: A no-arbitrage derivative pricing method that constructs replicating portfolios from electricity futures contracts rather than spot-market storage positions.

concepts.name: Non-storability of electricity
concepts.scope: The physical property of electricity that prevents inventory-based arbitrage and invalidates traditional commodity derivative pricing via cost-of-carry.

concepts.name: Geometric Brownian motion price process
concepts.scope: A continuous-time stochastic process with constant drift and volatility used as a baseline model for futures price dynamics.

concepts.name: Mean-reverting price process
concepts.scope: A stochastic process in which futures prices are pulled toward a long-run mean, capturing the empirically observed reversion in electricity prices.

concepts.name: Exchange option (Margrabe formula)
concepts.scope: An option giving the right to exchange one risky asset for another, representing a spread option with zero strike price.

concepts.name: Capacity right
concepts.scope: The right to convert a fixed quantity of fuel into electricity using a generation asset at a given point in time.

concepts.name: Real options valuation of generation assets
concepts.scope: Treating a power plant's operating flexibility as a portfolio of spark spread options integrated over the asset's remaining useful life.

concepts.name: Real options valuation of transmission assets
concepts.scope: Treating a transmission line as a pair of locational spread options permitting power flow in either direction less transmission costs.

concepts.name: Put-call parity for spread options
concepts.scope: A no-arbitrage relationship linking spark spread call and put values through the discounted difference of relevant futures prices.

concepts.name: No-arbitrage bounds for spread options
concepts.scope: Upper and lower limits on spark spread call values derived from the non-negativity of put prices and the bounded option payoff.

concepts.name: Implied market heat rate
concepts.scope: The ratio of the spot electricity price to the spot fuel price, representing the heat rate of the marginal generating unit under market conditions.

concepts.name: Volatility term structure
concepts.scope: The dependence of futures price volatility on contract maturity, modelled as a time-varying function calibrated to market data.

concepts.name: Discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation
concepts.scope: A traditional asset valuation method using risk-adjusted discounting of expected cash flows, used here as a benchmark against real options values.

methods: Closed-form option pricing via PDE solution
Margrabe exchange-option formula adapted to futures
Historical volatility estimation from NYMEX futures data
Integration of option values over asset lifetime for capacity valuation
Comparative statics analysis of option sensitivities

Statistical estimation of volatility from time series

framework_tseng.topic: Generation asset valuation using two-factor price lattices and real options

concepts.name: Real options for power plant valuation
concepts.scope: Treats the hourly commit/decommit decision of a generating unit as an American-type option exercised to maximise expected profit.

concepts.name: Spark spread
concepts.scope: Defines the net revenue from running a generator as electricity price minus heat-rate-weighted fuel price, framing plant operation as a spread option.

concepts.name: Two-factor correlated Itô price process
concepts.scope: Models electricity and fuel prices as two correlated continuous-time diffusion processes with general drift and constant volatility.

concepts.name: Mean-reverting (MR) process
concepts.scope: Specifies a stochastic process whose drift is Lipschitz-continuous, monotonically decreasing, and pushes the process back toward a long-run level.

concepts.name: Trinomial price lattice
concepts.scope: Discretises an Itô process onto a recombining three-branch lattice that matches local mean and variance at each node.

concepts.name: Two-factor trinomial lattice
concepts.scope: Extends the one-factor trinomial lattice to two correlated processes by branching each node into nine successor nodes with joint branching probabilities.

concepts.name: Lattice feasibility
concepts.scope: Requires that valid (non-negative, summing-to-one) branching probabilities exist at every node and every stage of the lattice.

concepts.name: Lattice compactness
concepts.scope: Property that the set of reachable lattice nodes remains bounded in size as the number of stages grows, enabled here by mean-reversion.

concepts.name: Lattice convergence
concepts.scope: Guarantees that the discrete joint distribution represented by the lattice approaches the true continuous distribution as the time-step tends to zero.

concepts.name: Decoupling transformation
concepts.scope: Linear change of variables that renders two correlated Itô processes into two uncorrelated processes, enabling independent one-factor lattice construction.

concepts.name: Branching probability selection via quadratic programme (QP)
concepts.scope: Chooses the nine joint branching probabilities at each node by minimising the squared deviation from the uncorrelated product probabilities, subject to moment-matching constraints.

concepts.name: Hull–White branching probability method
concepts.scope: Parameterises the correlation adjustment to the 3×3 probability matrix by a single scalar, as proposed by Hull and White (1994).

concepts.name: Lattice cell-size parameter (c)
concepts.scope: Constant scaling the node spacing relative to volatility and time-step, governing the trade-off between moment-matching quality and lattice feasibility.

concepts.name: Correlation feasibility bound ρ_max
concepts.scope: Derived upper bound on inter-process correlation below which the two-factor trinomial lattice is guaranteed feasible for any node and any stage.

concepts.name: Stochastic dynamic programming (SDP) for unit commitment
concepts.scope: Backward-recursive value function over the price lattice and unit commitment state, embedding minimum up/downtime and startup/shutdown cost constraints.

concepts.name: Unit commitment state space
concepts.scope: Encodes startup, normal-online, shutdown, and offline phases with minimum uptime/downtime constraints into an integer state variable.

concepts.name: Decision lead time constraint
concepts.scope: Requires that commit and decommit decisions be made a fixed number of hours before the corresponding operational state takes effect.

concepts.name: Variable heat rate
concepts.scope: Represents the fuel consumption per unit of electricity output as a function of generation level, affecting optimal dispatch and profit calculation.

concepts.name: Startup and shutdown costs
concepts.scope: One-time costs incurred at state transitions when a unit is brought online or taken offline, incorporated into the SDP transition cost function.

concepts.name: Optimal dispatch under price uncertainty
concepts.scope: Determines the generation level that maximises the spark-spread profit for a unit in the normal-online state given revealed electricity and fuel prices.

concepts.name: Risk-neutral vs. actual price process
concepts.scope: Distinguishes valuation under objective probability measure (actual process) from risk-neutral measure, with discussion of when forward-curve adjustments are needed.

concepts.name: Weak convergence of discrete approximations
concepts.scope: Invokes Kushner's theorem to establish that the trinomial lattice distribution converges weakly to the underlying Itô process as the number of stages grows.

concepts.name: Moment-matching for lattice construction
concepts.scope: Designs lattice branching probabilities to reproduce specified conditional moments (mean, variance, cross-moment) of the joint price distribution.

concepts.name: Sensitivity analysis of plant value
concepts.scope: Examines how the computed power plant value changes with respect to variations in price process parameters such as volatility, mean-reversion speed, and correlation.

concepts.name: Two-factor price lattice
concepts.scope: A discrete recombining lattice structure that jointly represents two correlated stochastic price processes for use in dynamic programming valuation.

concepts.name: Geometric mean reversion (GMR) process
concepts.scope: A continuous-time lognormal price process with mean-reverting drift, used to model electricity and fuel spot prices.

concepts.name: Branching probabilities
concepts.scope: Transition probabilities assigned to lattice branches so that local moments of the discrete chain match those of the underlying diffusion.

concepts.name: Branching factor
concepts.scope: An integer index that determines which of the three successor nodes a lattice branch points to at each time step.

concepts.name: Lattice cell size parameters (c1, c2)
concepts.scope: Scaling constants that set the spatial spacing of the lattice grid and control the maximum representable price correlation.

concepts.name: Optimization-based lattice calibration
concepts.scope: A derivative-free optimization procedure that selects cell size parameters to minimise the distance between the discrete lattice distribution and the target continuous density.

concepts.name: Moment matching
concepts.scope: A method of choosing branching probabilities by equating the first through fourth moments of the discrete distribution to those of the target diffusion.

concepts.name: Mean reversion property (MR property)
concepts.scope: A drift condition under which the one-factor lattice size remains bounded regardless of the number of time steps.

concepts.name: Generation asset valuation
concepts.scope: The determination of the economic value of a power plant by optimising dispatch decisions over a stochastic price lattice subject to physical operating constraints.

concepts.name: Unit commitment constraints
concepts.scope: Minimum uptime and downtime restrictions on a generating unit that introduce path-dependence into the dispatch optimisation.

concepts.name: Ramp constraints
concepts.scope: Limits on the rate of change of a generator's output between consecutive time periods.

concepts.name: Heat-rate function
concepts.scope: A convex function mapping generator output to fuel consumption, used to compute variable operating costs at each lattice node.

concepts.name: Stochastic dynamic programming (SDP)
concepts.scope: A backward-induction optimisation over the price lattice that computes the expected value of optimal future dispatch decisions.

concepts.name: Price correlation constraint
concepts.scope: A feasibility restriction on the lattice that caps the maximum representable instantaneous correlation between two price processes as a function of the cell size parameters.

concepts.name: Bivariate normal distribution fit
concepts.scope: The use of the exact bivariate normal density as a benchmark against which the lattice's discrete joint distribution is evaluated.

concepts.name: Time-dependent drift and volatility
concepts.scope: An extension of the lattice framework allowing drift and diffusion coefficients to vary by hour, accommodating peak/off-peak seasonality.

concepts.name: Forward-curve calibration for long-term valuation
concepts.scope: A procedure that sets the time-varying mean level of the mean-reversion process to reproduce observed forward price curves over multi-year horizons.

Linear transformation / decoupling of correlated Wiener processes
Quadratic programming for branching probability selection
Lattice size bounding via mean-reversion property

storage_value.topic: Hydro reservoir management in competitive electricity markets with long-term contracts

concepts.name: Hydro-thermal coordination
concepts.scope: Joint scheduling of hydro and thermal plant to minimise fuel and shortage costs over time.

concepts.name: Marginal water value
concepts.scope: Shadow price of stored water reflecting its opportunity cost in offsetting future thermal fuel expenditure.

concepts.name: Water value surface
concepts.scope: Multi-dimensional mapping of marginal water value as a function of reservoir storage level and time period.

concepts.name: Cournot oligopoly
concepts.scope: Strategic quantity-setting game among generating firms where each firm maximises profit taking rivals' quantities as given.

concepts.name: Supply Function Equilibrium (SFE)
concepts.scope: Nash equilibrium in which firms commit to price-quantity supply schedules rather than fixed prices or quantities.

concepts.name: Long-term financial contracts
concepts.scope: Forward or option contracts that fix a quantity at a strike price, altering firms' effective marginal revenue and output incentives.

concepts.name: Price Distortion Index (PDI)
concepts.scope: Metric quantifying the deviation of equilibrium spot price from the competitive marginal-cost benchmark.

concepts.name: Demand Curve for Release (DCR)
concepts.scope: Derived schedule mapping hydro release quantity to a range of marginal water values for use in DDP optimisation.

concepts.name: Dual Dynamic Programming (DDP)
concepts.scope: Dual variant of stochastic dynamic programming that iterates on marginal value functions rather than primal state trajectories to solve multi-period reservoir scheduling.

concepts.name: Stochastic inflows
concepts.scope: Random hydrological inflows to reservoirs modelled probabilistically to capture uncertainty in future water availability.

concepts.name: Competitive fringe
concepts.scope: Price-taking generators whose capacity is netted from market demand before strategic Cournot firms determine equilibrium output.

concepts.name: Reaction functions
concepts.scope: Best-response correspondences giving each firm's profit-maximising output as a function of rival firms' outputs.

concepts.name: Market Response Curve
concepts.scope: Aggregate equilibrium relationship between total market output and the exogenous marginal cost or water value parameter.

concepts.name: Consumer surplus
concepts.scope: Welfare measure capturing the difference between consumers' willingness to pay and the equilibrium spot price paid.

concepts.name: Constant elasticity demand curve
concepts.scope: Inverse demand specification in which price elasticity is constant at all output levels, used as an alternative to linear demand.

concepts.name: Linear demand curve
concepts.scope: Inverse demand specification with constant slope, yielding linear marginal revenue curves for strategic firms.

concepts.name: Storage trajectory
concepts.scope: Time path of reservoir storage levels generated by simulating operating rules derived from the DDP optimisation.

concepts.name: Perfect competition benchmark
concepts.scope: Reference case in which all firms price at marginal cost, used to measure efficiency losses under oligopolistic behaviour.

concepts.name: Medium-term scheduling
concepts.scope: Weekly-interval, annual-horizon optimisation of generation dispatch and reservoir releases given expected demand and inflows.

concepts.name: Market equilibrium
concepts.scope: Simultaneous solution of all firms' best-response conditions that clears the spot market at a single clearing price.

concepts.name: Dual Dynamic Programming (DSDP)
concepts.scope: Multi-period stochastic optimisation method for hydro reservoir scheduling that yields water value surfaces and operating guidelines.

concepts.name: Water value
concepts.scope: Marginal value of stored water in a reservoir, used as a shadow price to link hydro dispatch decisions across time.

concepts.name: Nash equilibrium
concepts.scope: Strategy profile in which no firm can increase its own profit by unilaterally deviating from its equilibrium action.

concepts.name: Supply function equilibrium
concepts.scope: Game-theoretic framework in which firms bid entire supply functions rather than scalar quantities or prices.

concepts.name: Two-way contract (contract for differences)
concepts.scope: Financial hedge in which a generator and consumer exchange payments based on the difference between the spot price and an agreed strike price on a fixed quantity.

concepts.name: Call option (back-up contract)
concepts.scope: One-way contract in which the seller compensates the buyer when the spot price exceeds the strike price on the contracted quantity.

concepts.name: Put option
concepts.scope: One-way contract in which the buyer compensates the seller when the spot price falls below the strike price on the contracted quantity.

concepts.name: Market response curve (MRC)
concepts.scope: Locus of Cournot Nash equilibrium price-quantity pairs traced out across a range of demand curves for a given period.

concepts.name: Reaction function
concepts.scope: Mapping that gives each firm's profit-maximising output as a function of the aggregate output of rival firms.

concepts.name: Linear inverse demand curve
concepts.scope: Demand specification expressing market price as an affine function of total generation, used to derive closed-form Cournot equilibria.

concepts.name: Price elasticity of demand
concepts.scope: Ratio of the proportional change in quantity demanded to the proportional change in price, used to parameterise demand curves.

concepts.name: Stepped marginal cost curve
concepts.scope: Piecewise-constant representation of a firm's marginal production cost as a function of output, derived from unit capacities and heat rates.

concepts.name: Admissible equilibrium solution
concepts.scope: A solved Cournot equilibrium point whose implied generation level falls within the generation range consistent with the assumed marginal cost segment.

concepts.name: Uniqueness of Cournot equilibrium
concepts.scope: Theoretical result establishing conditions—non-decreasing marginal costs and sufficiently elastic demand—under which exactly one Nash equilibrium exists.

concepts.name: Perfect competitor
concepts.scope: Generating firm that bids at true marginal cost and treats market price as exogenous, providing the welfare-benchmark dispatch.

concepts.name: Nett spot generation
concepts.scope: A firm's total generation minus its contracted quantity, determining whether it is a net buyer or seller in the spot market.

concepts.name: Dispatch market
concepts.scope: Half-hourly clearing mechanism in which generators submit stepped offer curves and purchasers submit bid curves to set dispatch quantities and prices.

concepts.name: Market share relationship
concepts.scope: Formula expressing each firm's equilibrium generation as an equal share adjusted for the deviation of its marginal cost from the industry average.

concepts.name: Single aggregate reservoir model
concepts.scope: Simplification that represents all hydro storage as one reservoir, ignoring spatial, transmission and head-effect complexities.

concepts.name: Reserve capacity market
concepts.scope: Ancillary-services market requiring plant capable of responding within specified times to cover unexpected generation failures.

concepts.name: Cournot oligopoly equilibrium
concepts.scope: A non-cooperative quantity-setting game solution where each firm maximises profit given rivals' outputs, used to determine spot-market generation and price.

concepts.name: Two-way (forward) contracts
concepts.scope: Financial instruments fixing a price for a quantity of electricity that reduce a firm's incentive to raise the spot price above its contract strike price.

concepts.name: Call (one-way / back-up) contracts
concepts.scope: Options transferring contract obligations from one firm to another when the spot price exceeds the strike price, affecting the effective contracting level of each firm.

concepts.name: Perfectly competitive (PC) benchmark
concepts.scope: The reference dispatch in which every station generates whenever its marginal cost is below the spot price, yielding the minimum-cost merit-order solution.

concepts.name: Merit order and plant portfolio effects
concepts.scope: The observation that a firm owning low-marginal-cost, large-capacity plant has greater ability to raise the spot price than a firm owning high-merit-order plant.

concepts.name: Demand elasticity sensitivity
concepts.scope: The dependence of market-power distortion on the slope of the demand curve, with less elastic (steeper) demand producing greater price mark-ups.

concepts.name: Demand Curve for Storage (DCS)
concepts.scope: A schedule mapping marginal water value to optimal end-of-period reservoir storage, derived recursively by aggregating the DCR with the future DCS and inflow distributions.

concepts.name: Stochastic inflow treatment
concepts.scope: Incorporation of uncertain future inflows as a discrete probability distribution, producing an expected DCS via probability-weighted averaging of shifted value curves.

concepts.name: Storage bounds and spill / shortage costs
concepts.scope: Physical upper and lower limits on reservoir storage that truncate the DCS at zero (spill) or a fixed shortage penalty (minimum storage), bounding marginal water values.

concepts.name: Market breakup / asset allocation
concepts.scope: The assignment of generation stations among competing firms, which determines each firm's portfolio, market share, and consequent ability to exercise market power.

concepts.name: Allocative vs productive efficiency trade-off
concepts.scope: The distinction between minimising total generation cost (productive efficiency) and maximising consumer surplus (allocative efficiency), which back-up contracts can affect in opposing directions.

concepts.name: Monopolist vs price-taker mixed market
concepts.scope: A market structure where one firm acts as a Cournot monopolist and the other dispatches competitively, producing non-monotone MRCs and soft price caps at each competitive firm's marginal cost step.

concepts.name: Load Duration Curve (LDC)
concepts.scope: A representation of electricity demand ranked by level over a period, used to weight generation decisions and translate single-period results to a longer planning horizon.

concepts.name: Water Value Surface (WVS)
concepts.scope: A two-dimensional surface mapping the marginal value of stored water as a function of storage level and time period.

concepts.name: Marginal Water Value (MWV)
concepts.scope: The shadow price of water in storage, used as the effective fuel cost of hydro generation in dispatch decisions.

concepts.name: Cournot duopoly with competitive fringe
concepts.scope: A single-period market model where two strategic firms choose quantities simultaneously alongside a price-taking fringe.

concepts.name: Forward/financial contracts and back-up contracts
concepts.scope: Pre-committed energy obligations that alter firm incentives, reducing price distortion as contract coverage increases toward 100%.

concepts.name: Stochastic inflow uncertainty
concepts.scope: Random variation in reservoir inflows handled by probability-weighted averaging of shifted DCSs within the DDP framework.

concepts.name: Merit order and hydro scheduling
concepts.scope: The ranking of generation units by marginal cost, with MWV determining where hydro sits relative to thermal plant in dispatch.

concepts.name: Reservoir storage bounds and spill risk
concepts.scope: Physical limits on reservoir capacity that constrain optimal release policy and create spill risk at low contract levels.

concepts.name: Demand elasticity
concepts.scope: The price-responsiveness of electricity demand, which governs the magnitude of price distortion in the Cournot market model.

concepts.name: Consumer and producer surplus
concepts.scope: Welfare measures used to evaluate outcomes across different contracting regimes and market structures.

concepts.name: Load duration curve (LDC) sub-period modelling
concepts.scope: Representation of intra-period demand variation via sub-periods whose DCRs are combined as a convex-weighted average.

concepts.name: Monotonicity of DCR and DCS
concepts.scope: Theoretical property guaranteeing that both the demand curve for release and the demand curve for storage are non-increasing, ensuring DDP validity.

concepts.name: Forward contracts
concepts.scope: Financial instruments committing generators to supply electricity at pre-agreed prices, including one-way and two-way variants as well as put and call options.

concepts.name: Hydro reservoir scheduling
concepts.scope: Optimal inter-temporal allocation of water releases from reservoirs to generate electricity subject to inflow uncertainty.

concepts.name: Stochastic dynamic programming
concepts.scope: A recursive optimisation framework for sequential decision-making under uncertainty, applied here to reservoir release scheduling.

concepts.name: Oligopoly pricing
concepts.scope: Strategic price or quantity setting by a small number of electricity generating firms, encompassing Cournot and Bertrand solution concepts.

concepts.name: Cournot outcome
concepts.scope: A Nash equilibrium in quantities resulting from capacity precommitment followed by price competition, as in the Kreps-Scheinkman framework.

concepts.name: Back-up capacity
concepts.scope: Thermal generation capacity available as a competitive fringe or fallback supply that constrains the market power of hydro-thermal incumbents.

concepts.name: Energy spot price
concepts.scope: The short-run market-clearing price for electricity in each period, determined by aggregate supply and demand.

concepts.name: Profit distribution
concepts.scope: The mean and variance of firm-level revenues net of costs across Monte Carlo or stochastic simulation draws.

concepts.name: Storage level
concepts.scope: The volume of water held in a reservoir at each time step, linking current decisions to future generation capacity.

concepts.name: Correlated inflows
concepts.scope: Statistical dependence across time or across reservoirs in the random water inflow process, affecting multi-period scheduling.

concepts.name: Deregulated electricity market
concepts.scope: A restructured power sector in which generation is exposed to competitive market forces rather than regulated monopoly dispatch.

concepts.name: Quantity precommitment
concepts.scope: A first-stage capacity or output commitment that shapes subsequent price competition and can yield Cournot-equivalent outcomes.

concepts.name: Biases in stochastic reservoir models
concepts.scope: Systematic errors arising from discretisation or approximation in stochastic DP models for hydro scheduling.

concepts.name: Total contract quantity
concepts.scope: The aggregate volume of forward contracts written by generators, used as the key independent variable in the simulation sensitivity analysis.

concepts.name: contract quantity
concepts.scope: The total volume of forward or bilateral contracts written, used as a key parameter varying across simulation scenarios.

concepts.name: mean-variance analysis of market outcomes
concepts.scope: Statistical characterisation of equilibrium variables by their means and standard deviations across stochastic realisations.

concepts.name: multi-period market equilibrium
concepts.scope: An equilibrium concept spanning several time periods in which storage decisions link current and future market outcomes.

methods: Linear and constant-elasticity demand curve fitting
Monte Carlo simulation of inflow scenarios
Implicit differentiation of first-order conditions to derive reaction function slopes
Piecewise-linear marginal cost partitioning for admissibility search
Closed-form equilibrium solution under linear demand
Polynomial root-finding for equilibrium price under constant elasticity demand
Reaction function analysis for uniqueness proofs (Tirole stability condition)
Cournot game solution across parameterised demand curves
Aggregation of demand curves along quantity axis
Discrete stochastic inflow averaging for expected DCS
Numerical solution of constant-elasticity Cournot equilibrium
Closed-form solution of linear-demand Cournot equilibrium
Sensitivity analysis over elasticity and contracting levels
Comparative static analysis of asset allocation options
Cournot equilibrium computation (linear and constant-elasticity demand)
Stochastic dynamic programming with probability-weighted inflow scenarios
Water value surface construction by backward recursion
Merit-order dispatch with MWV as shadow fuel cost
Convex combination of sub-period demand curves
Sensitivity analysis over contract levels and demand elasticities
Model calibration via iterative marginal water value estimation
Sensitivity analysis over demand elasticity and contract quantity
Statistical reporting of means and standard deviations
Monte Carlo sampling of market outcomes
mean and standard deviation computation of endogenous variables

Microeconomic theory of oligopoly and Cournot competition
Financial derivatives: forwards and call options

tseng_barz_short_term_generation_asset_v.topic: Short-term generation asset valuation with unit commitment constraints using real options

concepts.name: Spark spread option
concepts.scope: The payoff of a power plant modelled as a call option on the spread between electricity price and heat-rate-weighted fuel price.

concepts.name: Unit commitment constraints
concepts.scope: Physical operating rules—minimum uptime, minimum downtime, startup/shutdown lead times—that restrict when a thermal generator can change its on/off state.

concepts.name: Minimum uptime and downtime
concepts.scope: Requirements that once a thermal unit is started or stopped it must remain in that state for a specified minimum number of periods.

concepts.name: Startup and shutdown costs
concepts.scope: Economic costs incurred when switching a unit between offline and online states, including fuel and labour components that vary with boiler cooling state.

concepts.name: State variable for unit commitment
concepts.scope: A signed integer tracking whether a unit is online or offline and how many periods it has been in that mode.

concepts.name: Indifference locus (IL)
concepts.scope: The boundary in the (electricity price, fuel price) plane at which the expected profit from committing versus not committing a unit is equal.

concepts.name: Multistage stochastic dynamic programming
concepts.scope: A backward-recursive optimisation framework that embeds price uncertainty into sequential unit-commitment decisions over a planning horizon.

concepts.name: Forward Monte Carlo simulation
concepts.scope: Price-path generation moving forward in time used within the backward dynamic programming to evaluate expected future values.

concepts.name: Geometric mean-reverting price process
concepts.scope: A continuous-time Ito process for electricity or fuel prices with mean reversion and lognormally distributed levels used to capture observed market dynamics.

concepts.name: Heat rate
concepts.scope: The conversion ratio (MMBtu/MWh) between fuel consumed and electricity generated, represented as a quadratic function of output level.

concepts.name: Optimal dispatch
concepts.scope: Real-time selection of generation output to maximise instantaneous profit subject to capacity bounds, solved analytically given current prices.

concepts.name: Ramp rate constraint
concepts.scope: A limit on how quickly a generator can change its output level between consecutive online periods.

concepts.name: Analytical upper bound on plant value
concepts.scope: A relaxed formulation with no minimum uptime/downtime or startup costs that yields a closed-form overestimate of true plant value.

concepts.name: Financial options approach to plant valuation
concepts.scope: Prior literature method that values a power plant as a strip of European spark-spread call options, ignoring operational constraints.

concepts.name: Spinning reserve market
concepts.scope: An ancillary-service capacity market where an online unit can sell residual capacity below its rated maximum.

concepts.name: No-load cost
concepts.scope: The fixed fuel cost component required to keep a thermal unit online at zero power output.

concepts.name: Risk-neutral vs actual price processes
concepts.scope: Distinction between market-implied risk-neutral distributions used in derivatives pricing and historical statistical distributions used for operational valuation.

concepts.name: Maximum likelihood estimation for price processes
concepts.scope: Statistical procedure for fitting mean-reversion rate, volatility and seasonality parameters of log-price processes to historical data.

concepts.name: State-transition diagram
concepts.scope: A graphical representation of feasible transitions between unit operating states governed by uptime, downtime and lead-time constraints.

concepts.name: Boiler cooling function
concepts.scope: An exponential model describing how startup cost varies with the duration a unit has been offline as the boiler loses heat.

concepts.name: Real options valuation
concepts.scope: Treating generation asset operational flexibility as financial options to derive economic value.

concepts.name: Spark spread options
concepts.scope: Options on the spread between electricity prices and fuel costs used to value and hedge power plant output.

concepts.name: Stochastic differential equations
concepts.scope: Continuous-time probabilistic models governing the dynamics of electricity and fuel prices.

concepts.name: Unit commitment
concepts.scope: Short-term scheduling problem determining which generating units to commit subject to operational constraints.

concepts.name: Ramp constraints
concepts.scope: Physical limits on the rate of change of generator output incorporated into short-term scheduling.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo simulation for path-dependent options
concepts.scope: Simulation-based pricing method extended to handle options whose payoffs depend on the full price path.

concepts.name: Two-factor price lattices
concepts.scope: Discrete lattice framework incorporating two stochastic price factors for generation asset valuation.

concepts.name: Nodal pricing and transmission rights
concepts.scope: Locational marginal pricing and associated financial rights capturing the value of transmission capacity.

concepts.name: Electricity derivatives pricing and risk management
concepts.scope: Valuation and hedging of derivative instruments written on electricity prices in competitive markets.

concepts.name: Options on futures spreads
concepts.scope: Financial options whose underlying is the spread between two futures contracts, applied to energy commodities.

methods: Analytical upper-bound derivation via constraint relaxation
Financial options theory applied to physical assets
implied_prerequisites: Electricity market structure and spot pricing

kyhydropumpinput.topic: Hydro pump storage valuation model input configuration

concepts.name: Hydro pump storage
concepts.scope: Parametric setup for a pumped-hydro storage asset including capacity, efficiency, and operational horizon.

concepts.name: Storage efficiency (round-trip)
concepts.scope: Ratio capturing energy losses when pumping and generating, here set at 0.8.

concepts.name: EEX price curve
concepts.scope: Forward or spot price schedule from the European Energy Exchange used as the underlying price process.

concepts.name: Least-Squares Monte Carlo (LSMC)
concepts.scope: Simulation-based dynamic-programming method for valuing the optimal dispatch of a storage asset.

concepts.name: Operational date range
concepts.scope: Start and end dates (encoded as Excel serial numbers) defining the asset's active dispatch window.

concepts.name: Reservoir capacity and inventory
concepts.scope: Maximum storage level and initial fill state constraining feasible pump/generate decisions at each time step.

concepts.name: Simulation paths
concepts.scope: Number of Monte Carlo scenarios (50) drawn to approximate the value function via LSMC regression.

concepts.name: Pump-storage hydro asset
concepts.scope: A two-reservoir hydroelectric facility that can both generate and consume electricity by pumping water between an upper and lower storage.

concepts.name: Top/bottom storage configuration
concepts.scope: The physical representation of upper and lower reservoirs, including initial volumes and maximum capacities.

concepts.name: Initial volume assumption
concepts.scope: A fallback rule setting the lower reservoir's starting volume as the upper reservoir's maximum capacity minus its initial storage when the lower reservoir is undefined.

concepts.name: Intrinsic valuation
concepts.scope: Deterministic valuation of the storage asset based on known or forward price spreads without simulation of price uncertainty.

concepts.name: Simulation valuation
concepts.scope: Stochastic valuation of the storage asset using Monte Carlo or equivalent price path simulation to capture optionality.

concepts.name: Valuation horizon
concepts.scope: The start and end dates over which the asset is valued, here a single calendar month.

0109_electricity_price_modelling_for_pro.topic: Electricity price modelling for Profit at Risk management

concepts.name: Profit at Risk (PaR)
concepts.scope: A risk measure describing the worst expected operational profit to a specified confidence level over a given period, analogous to VaR but applied to physical-asset portfolios.

concepts.name: Value at Risk (VaR)
concepts.scope: A financial-industry risk measure that PaR is derived from, representing the worst expected loss at a given confidence level.

concepts.name: Spot price modelling
concepts.scope: Representation of electricity spot price dynamics via stochastic differential equations separating deterministic and stochastic components.

concepts.name: Regime-switching price model
concepts.scope: A two-regime framework distinguishing a normal price state from a spike state, governed by a Markov transition matrix.

concepts.name: Mean reversion
concepts.scope: A property of commodity price processes whereby prices tend to revert to a long-run mean, captured by a mean-reversion parameter κ.

concepts.name: Price spikes
concepts.scope: Short-lived extreme price deviations in electricity markets modelled as a separate regime with its own mean and variance.

concepts.name: Seasonal and calendar effects
concepts.scope: Deterministic components of the price model capturing monthly and day-of-week price patterns via dummy variables.

concepts.name: Forward price curve
concepts.scope: The term structure of forward electricity prices used for calibration of price scenarios and as hedge instrument pricing.

concepts.name: Spark spread option
concepts.scope: A representation of a thermal power plant's operational value as an option on the spread between electricity price and fuel/variable cost.

concepts.name: Hedging with forward contracts
concepts.scope: The use of short forward positions to reduce portfolio profit variability and satisfy a PaR constraint.

concepts.name: Volume risk
concepts.scope: Uncertainty in power plant output arising from forced outages, modelled as a Markov two-state availability process.

concepts.name: Correlation between price spikes and forced outages
concepts.scope: The dependence between simultaneous high-price events and plant unavailability, captured through a joint transition matrix.

concepts.name: Financial price models
concepts.scope: Econometric models using historical spot and derivative market data to parameterise stochastic processes for electricity prices.

concepts.name: Fundamental price models
concepts.scope: Bottom-up engineering models that derive electricity prices from supply, demand, transmission, and cost data.

concepts.name: Combined price modelling approach
concepts.scope: A hybrid methodology that uses fundamental models to generate price scenarios then calibrates them to observed forward prices.

concepts.name: Kurtosis-based recursive filter
concepts.scope: An iterative spike-identification procedure that removes data points until sample kurtosis is within a specified ratio of normal-distribution kurtosis.

concepts.name: Hydrological risk
concepts.scope: Uncertainty in annual electricity prices driven by variation in hydro reservoir inflows between wet and dry years.

concepts.name: Input model risk
concepts.scope: The risk that errors in the parameterisation or structural choices of input models distort the optimal solution of a decision problem.

concepts.name: Mixed integer programming
concepts.scope: An optimisation framework used to solve the PaR maximisation and minimisation problems arising from the non-convex structure of the PaR measure.

concepts.name: Pay-off diagram
concepts.scope: A graphical representation of portfolio profit as a function of electricity price, used to analyse the effect of hedging on PaR.

slides_for_13_april_2017_ne_deep_dive_fi.topic: Energy Storage Technologies, Applications and Economics for Power Markets

concepts.name: Electricity storage technology taxonomy
concepts.scope: Classification of storage technologies into five classes: mechanical, chemical, thermal, molecular, and electrical, with sub-categories for each.

concepts.name: System services framework
concepts.scope: Categorisation of storage applications into stability, capacity, and energy services, differentiated by discharge time and required power rating.

concepts.name: Power-to-energy ratio
concepts.scope: The inherent ratio of rated power to stored energy capacity that characterises each storage technology and determines its natural service match.

concepts.name: Use-case stacking
concepts.scope: The practice of dispatching a single storage installation to provide multiple non-coincident services to capture incremental revenue streams.

concepts.name: Behind-the-meter storage
concepts.scope: Storage sited on the customer side of the utility meter to reduce demand charges, integrate distributed PV, or improve power quality.

concepts.name: Energy arbitrage
concepts.scope: The strategy of charging storage during low-price periods and discharging during high-price periods to capture wholesale price spreads.

concepts.name: Ancillary services
concepts.scope: Grid-stability products such as frequency regulation procured by system operators and valued on a per-kW basis.

concepts.name: Levelised cost of storage (LCoS)
concepts.scope: A cost metric analogous to LCOE that captures total lifecycle costs per unit of energy delivered by a storage asset, with strong dependence on use case and duration.

concepts.name: Storage CAPEX components
concepts.scope: Breakdown of installed battery system cost into battery pack, inverter, balance of plant, EPC, and energy management system elements.

concepts.name: Technology learning curves
concepts.scope: Empirical cost-reduction trajectories for storage technologies as cumulative deployed capacity increases, analogous to solar PV experience curves.

concepts.name: Flexibility supply curve
concepts.scope: A conceptual merit-order ranking of grid flexibility resources by cost and volume, showing how storage competes with demand response, interconnectors, and thermal generation.

concepts.name: Microgrid integration
concepts.scope: The combined operation of distributed PV, battery storage, and dispatchable generation in an islanded or semi-islanded configuration to provide reliable local power.

concepts.name: Demand response
concepts.scope: Automated or manual curtailment or shifting of electrical loads to provide grid flexibility, competing directly with stationary storage on cost.

concepts.name: Market structure and storage economics
concepts.scope: The influence of wholesale market design, price volatility, ancillary service rates, and regulatory environment on the financial viability of storage projects.

concepts.name: NPV-based storage project economics
concepts.scope: Project valuation methodology using discounted cash flows driven by revenue from energy shifting and ancillary services net of capital and operating costs.

concepts.name: Li-ion chemistry variants
concepts.scope: Sub-types of lithium-ion batteries differentiated by active cathode material (LFP, NCM, NCA, LCO, LTO, LMO) with distinct energy density and cycle-life trade-offs.

concepts.name: Pumped hydro storage (PHS)
concepts.scope: Mature large-scale mechanical storage technology using elevation difference to store and release energy, serving as the baseline long-duration storage benchmark.

concepts.name: Compressed air energy storage (CAES)
concepts.scope: Bulk mechanical storage technology compressing air into underground caverns, available in conventional, adiabatic, and isothermal variants.

concepts.name: Flow batteries
concepts.scope: Electrochemical storage systems where energy is stored in liquid electrolytes circulated through a cell stack, suited to longer-duration applications.

concepts.name: Variable renewable energy (vRES) integration
concepts.scope: Use of storage and other flexibility resources to absorb output variability and forecast error from wind and solar generation.

methods: Cash flow modelling for storage revenue and capex break-even analysis
NPV-based project economic modelling using forward price curves
Sensitivity / tornado analysis of key value drivers
Technology performance mapping on power-rating vs discharge-time axes
Market screening via wholesale price volatility and ancillary service rate analysis
Battery cost component decomposition and learning-curve projection
Techno-economic sizing of PV-storage-gas hybrid systems
Field data analysis for battery state-of-charge and ramp-rate performance
implied_prerequisites: Basic electricity market structure (wholesale, ancillary services, capacity markets)
Power system fundamentals (frequency regulation, grid stability, T&D)
Discounted cash flow and NPV analysis
Renewable energy generation characteristics (wind and solar variability)

storage_introduction_document_170413.topic: Electrical Energy Storage: technologies, system services, and economics

concepts.name: Energy arbitrage
concepts.scope: Shifting electricity from low-price periods to high-price periods to capture wholesale price spreads.

concepts.name: System services
concepts.scope: Grid-level services provided by storage covering stabilization (seconds-minutes), capacity (minutes-hours), and supply/demand shift (hours).

concepts.name: Power-to-energy ratio
concepts.scope: The ratio of rated power (kW) to energy capacity (kWh) that characterises the discharge duration of a storage technology.

concepts.name: Stabilization services
concepts.scope: Short-duration (seconds-minutes) ancillary services that continuously match supply and demand to maintain power quality and frequency.

concepts.name: Capacity services
concepts.scope: Medium-duration (minutes-hours) services that provide dispatchable power capacity to the system when needed.

concepts.name: Supply/demand shift
concepts.scope: Long-duration (hours) services that move energy from surplus periods to deficit periods to improve the match between variable supply and demand.

concepts.name: Pumped Hydro Storage (PHS)
concepts.scope: Mature, geography-constrained bulk storage technology currently the dominant deployed EES capacity worldwide.

concepts.name: Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES)
concepts.scope: Demonstrated large-scale mechanical storage technology that has seen limited efficiency improvement over several decades.

concepts.name: Lithium-ion batteries
concepts.scope: High-power-to-energy-ratio electrochemical storage technology currently cost-competitive primarily for short-duration stabilization services.

concepts.name: Flow batteries
concepts.scope: Electrochemical storage technology with decoupled power and energy ratings suited to longer-duration load-shifting applications.

concepts.name: Levelized Cost of Storage (LCoS)
concepts.scope: A first-order metric expressing the total lifecycle cost of providing a storage service in $/MWh to enable cross-technology comparison.

concepts.name: CAPEX thresholds
concepts.scope: Technology-cost benchmarks (in $/kWh installed) below which a storage technology becomes cost-competitive for a given service category.

concepts.name: Service stacking (value stacking)
concepts.scope: Delivering multiple system services from a single storage installation to maximise revenue and reduce dependence on any single income stream.

concepts.name: Demand response
concepts.scope: Load-side flexibility option that competes with EES in providing certain system services.

concepts.name: Interconnectors
concepts.scope: Transmission links between regions that act as competing flexibility resources to storage for cross-border energy balancing.

concepts.name: Variable renewable energy (VRE) integration
concepts.scope: The challenge of accommodating non-dispatchable wind and solar output within the power system, driving demand for flexibility services.

concepts.name: Behind-the-meter storage
concepts.scope: Customer-sited storage whose value derives from reducing grid-interaction costs such as peak demand charges, explicitly excluded from the main analysis.

concepts.name: Round-trip efficiency
concepts.scope: The ratio of energy discharged to energy charged, determining parasitic losses and charging costs over a storage cycle.

concepts.name: Module scale
concepts.scope: The physical and power/energy size of a single deployable storage unit, affecting geographic flexibility and grid connection level.

concepts.name: Battery pack vs. total installed cost
concepts.scope: The distinction between cell/module costs and full system costs, where battery pack costs represent approximately half of total installed cost.

System perspective vs. project perspective framing
