dipeng_supply.topic: Corporate renewable electricity procurement and PPA structuring

concepts.name: Power Purchase Agreement (PPA)
concepts.scope: Long-term contract between a renewable energy generator and a buyer specifying volume, price, and delivery terms for electricity.

concepts.name: Guarantee of Origin (GoO / GvO)
concepts.scope: Tradeable certificate attesting that a specified quantity of electricity was generated from a renewable source.

concepts.name: Additionaliteit (Additionality)
concepts.scope: Requirement that procured renewable electricity or GoOs originate from generation capacity newly built as a result of the procurement commitment.

concepts.name: Uurmatching (Hourly matching)
concepts.scope: Alignment of renewable electricity generation with consumption on an hour-by-hour basis rather than on an annual volume basis.

concepts.name: Balancing Responsible Party / Programme Responsible Party (PRP)
concepts.scope: Party responsible for nominating generation schedules and managing imbalance between contracted and actual electricity volumes in the grid.

concepts.name: Baseload block delivery
concepts.scope: Conversion of a variable wind-generation profile into a flat (baseload) volume block by a PRP, simplifying portfolio integration for the supplier.

concepts.name: Imbalance risk
concepts.scope: Financial exposure arising from deviations between forecast and actual electricity consumption or generation settled against the spot market.

concepts.name: APX / EPEX spot market
concepts.scope: Day-ahead and intraday power exchange serving as the settlement reference for uncontracted electricity volumes.

concepts.name: ENDEX (TTF/power forward market)
concepts.scope: Forward market used to fix electricity prices ahead of the delivery year, contrasted with spot procurement.

concepts.name: SDE+ subsidy (Stimulering Duurzame Energieproductie)
concepts.scope: Dutch feed-in premium scheme providing a floor price for renewable electricity producers, with an associated correction mechanism affecting GoO pricing.

concepts.name: CertiQ
concepts.scope: Dutch registry operator for Guarantees of Origin where GoOs are issued, transferred, and cancelled on behalf of producers and end-users.

concepts.name: Market-to-market (MtM) exposure
concepts.scope: Mark-to-market valuation of open forward positions representing the current gain or loss if positions were closed at prevailing market prices.

concepts.name: Supply chain financing
concepts.scope: Financing arrangement allowing extended buyer payment terms while suppliers receive early payment via a third-party financier at a defined interest rate.

concepts.name: Full supply agreement
concepts.scope: Contract under which a single supplier is responsible for meeting the entire electricity demand of specified sites including balancing and ancillary services.

concepts.name: GoO unbundled supply (Part B)
concepts.scope: Procurement of Guarantees of Origin separately from physical electricity delivery, used to green sites without a dedicated grid connection.

concepts.name: Sleeving
concepts.scope: Intermediary service in which a supplier absorbs renewable generation into its portfolio and delivers equivalent volume to the off-taker under a standard supply contract.

concepts.name: European Renewable Energy Directive
concepts.scope: EU regulatory framework setting renewable energy targets and defining rules for Guarantees of Origin and renewable electricity claims.

concepts.name: Market coupling
concepts.scope: Integration of adjacent power spot markets enabling cross-border capacity allocation and price convergence, relevant to GoO geography eligibility.

concepts.name: Capacity factor
concepts.scope: Ratio of actual electricity output to maximum possible output over a period, used to estimate annual PPA volume from wind parks.

concepts.name: Tender / RFP process
concepts.scope: Structured competitive procurement procedure through which a corporate buyer solicits and evaluates supplier proposals for a long-term energy contract.

concepts.name: Guarantee of Origin (GoO)
concepts.scope: Tradeable certificate attesting that a specified quantity of electricity was generated from a renewable source, used to substantiate green claims.

concepts.name: Full supply contract
concepts.scope: Electricity supply arrangement under which the supplier covers all consumption at a site, including balancing and program responsibility.

concepts.name: Program responsibility
concepts.scope: Obligation to maintain a balanced electricity portfolio on behalf of a market participant, transferred here from buyer to supplier.

concepts.name: Baseload block
concepts.scope: Fixed-volume flat electricity product covering every hour of a defined period, purchased on forward markets or via supplier quote.

concepts.name: APX/EPEX spot price
concepts.scope: Volume-weighted average of hourly day-ahead auction prices on the Dutch or Belgian power exchange used to settle residual consumption.

concepts.name: Volume-weighted average price
concepts.scope: Price benchmark calculated by weighting each traded price by its associated volume, applied here to baseload fixations.

concepts.name: Supplier fee
concepts.scope: Fixed all-inclusive charge in €/MWh covering balancing, program responsibility, invoicing and other supply services.

concepts.name: Hourly matching
concepts.scope: Approach to renewable electricity procurement that aligns GoO cancellation or generation with actual consumption on an hour-by-hour basis.

concepts.name: Additionality
concepts.scope: Requirement that renewable electricity projects qualify only if their first generation occurs within the term of the supply agreement.

concepts.name: CertiQ / VREG registry
concepts.scope: National registries in the Netherlands and Belgium respectively where GoOs are issued, transferred and cancelled on behalf of end users.

concepts.name: Regulated contributions (green and CHP certificates)
concepts.scope: Mandatory levies in Belgium related to groenestroomcertificaten and warmtekrachtcertificaten that suppliers pass through transparently to buyers.

concepts.name: Net losses (Elia)
concepts.scope: Transmission losses charged by the Belgian TSO Elia that are invoiced separately as a regulated cost item.

concepts.name: EAN code
concepts.scope: Unique identifier for an electricity connection point used to define the scope of individual supply agreements.

concepts.name: Supply Chain Financing (Global Confirming)
concepts.scope: Third-party bank facility that allows suppliers to receive early payment against approved invoices at a cost linked to the buyer's credit rating.

concepts.name: PPA portfolio integration
concepts.scope: Mechanism by which wind-park output delivered by a program responsible party is merged into a supplier's retail portfolio and allocated across buyer sites.

concepts.name: RE100 commitment
concepts.scope: Corporate pledge to source 100% of electricity consumption from renewable sources, used here to define procurement targets and timelines.

concepts.name: Framework Agreement
concepts.scope: Master contract governing overarching terms between buyer and supplier, under which individual site supply agreements are concluded.

concepts.name: Power Export Purchase and Sales Agreement (PEPSA)
concepts.scope: Contract governing the sale of surplus electricity exported from an embedded CHP generator to a licensed supplier.

concepts.name: Power Import Purchase and Sales Agreement (PIPSA)
concepts.scope: Contract governing the purchase of electricity imported from the grid to meet on-site demand.

concepts.name: Embedded Generation
concepts.scope: Generation connected to the distribution network rather than the transmission system, giving rise to avoided network charges and other financial benefits.

concepts.name: Embedded Benefits
concepts.scope: Financial savings accruing to a supplier from hosting a generator on the distribution network, including avoided DUoS and TNUoS charges.

concepts.name: Triad Avoidance
concepts.scope: Revenue or cost savings arising from generating during the three half-hours of highest system demand used to set TNUoS demand charges.

concepts.name: Generator Distribution Use of System Charges (GDUoS)
concepts.scope: Charges (positive or negative) levied on generators connected to the distribution network, reflecting locational network costs.

concepts.name: Distribution Use of System Charges (DUoS)
concepts.scope: Charges paid by suppliers and consumers for use of the electricity distribution network.

concepts.name: Balancing Services Use of System (BSUoS) Charges
concepts.scope: Transmission-level charges recovered by National Grid for balancing the system, potentially avoided by embedded generators.

concepts.name: Combined Heat and Power (CHP) Plant
concepts.scope: Co-generation facility producing both electrical power and useful heat, here fuelled by LNG boil-off gas.

concepts.name: Good Quality CHP Status
concepts.scope: CHPQA designation qualifying a plant for Climate Change Levy exemptions and other regulatory benefits.

concepts.name: Climate Change Levy (CCL) Directed Utility Status
concepts.scope: Regulatory classification allowing an entity to account for CCL on behalf of itself and sub-customers.

concepts.name: Day-Ahead and Within-Day Nominations
concepts.scope: Processes by which a generator or consumer notifies the supplier of expected export or import volumes for scheduling and pricing.

concepts.name: Imbalance / Balancing Exposure
concepts.scope: Financial risk arising when actual metered generation or consumption differs from nominated volumes under the BSC settlement regime.

concepts.name: Maximum Import/Export Capacity (MIC/MEC)
concepts.scope: Contractual limits on the volume of power that can be imported or exported through a grid connection, set seasonally.

concepts.name: Meter Point Administration Number (MPAN)
concepts.scope: Unique identifier for an electricity supply point used in registration and settlement systems.

concepts.name: Supply Meter Registration Service (SMRS)
concepts.scope: Industry system in which suppliers register metering points for settlement purposes.

concepts.name: EU Emissions Trading Scheme (EU-ETS) Participation
concepts.scope: Regulatory obligation for large emitters to hold and surrender carbon allowances for CO2 emissions.

concepts.name: Credit Support in Power Supply Contracts
concepts.scope: Collateral or guarantee arrangements required between counterparties to mitigate payment default risk.

concepts.name: Demand-Side Management (DSM)
concepts.scope: Flexible adjustment of electricity consumption or generation in response to grid signals or price incentives.

concepts.name: Imbalance Price and Settlement
concepts.scope: BSC mechanism determining the cash-out price for energy deviations between contracted and metered volumes.

concepts.name: Collar / Floor / Option Structures for Power Price Risk
concepts.scope: Derivative instruments used to bound or floor the effective price received for generated electricity.

concepts.name: Portfolio Balancing and Return on Credit
concepts.scope: Assessment of how aggregating multiple generation or demand assets reduces net imbalance exposure and improves credit efficiency.

methods: Request for Proposal (RFP) with Q&A process
GoO cancellation accounting via CertiQ end-user account
Competitive tender / request for proposal process
Volume-weighted average price calculation for baseload fixations
Monthly baseload block scheduling from PPA output
Proportional GoO allocation across sites by consumption share
Spot-price settlement of residual consumption (APX/EPEX hourly)
Multi-part lot structure allowing separate or combined award
Scenario analysis (CHP-on vs re-liquefaction plant operational)
Triad period identification and payment calculation
Proforma invoice construction with supporting metering data
implied_prerequisites: Basic electricity market structure (wholesale, balancing, retail)
Corporate procurement and contract law basics
Dutch and Belgian electricity regulatory frameworks
Basic electricity market structure (generation, transmission, retail)
Understanding of day-ahead and forward power markets
Familiarity with European renewable energy certificate schemes
Concept of balancing and imbalance settlement
GB electricity market structure (BSC, CUSC, DNO/TNO roles)
CHP and embedded generation technology basics

dipeng_swing.topic: Swing contract pricing and optimisation (gas and power)

concepts.name: Swing option
concepts.scope: A commodity derivative granting the holder the right to vary daily take quantities within contractual limits over a delivery period.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo simulation for swing valuation
concepts.scope: Stochastic simulation of price paths used to estimate the expected value of swing exercise strategies.

concepts.name: Play optimisation
concepts.scope: Determination of the optimal exercise strategy for a swing contract given simulated forward price scenarios.

concepts.name: Market-to-market / mark-to-market (MA-DA) valuation
concepts.scope: Daily valuation of swing positions by comparing market price to contract strike across historical periods.

concepts.name: Fixed random-number simulation
concepts.scope: Use of a fixed random seed or pre-drawn random numbers to ensure reproducibility of Monte Carlo paths.

concepts.name: Gas swing standalone model
concepts.scope: Self-contained valuation model for natural gas swing contracts without cross-commodity linkage.

concepts.name: Power swing standalone model
concepts.scope: Self-contained valuation model for electricity swing contracts without cross-commodity linkage.

concepts.name: NBP price history
concepts.scope: Historical National Balancing Point gas spot and forward price data used as model inputs.

concepts.name: ICE Heren price data
concepts.scope: Exchange-sourced forward curve data for natural gas used in historical back-valuation of swing contracts.

dipeng_team_meeting.topic: Dutch and German power spark spread options: valuation, hedging and market challenges

concepts.name: Clean Spark Spread
concepts.scope: The margin from generating power from gas after accounting for fuel cost and carbon cost.

concepts.name: Spark Spread Call Option
concepts.scope: An option giving the right to receive the positive difference between power price and gas-equivalent cost above a strike.

concepts.name: Spark Spread Put Option
concepts.scope: An option giving the right to receive the positive difference between a strike and the spark spread, used here out-of-the-money.

concepts.name: Daily Optionality
concepts.scope: The additional value arising from the ability to exercise an option on a daily rather than a period-average basis.

concepts.name: Index Discount with Floor
concepts.scope: A pricing structure where the underlying index is reduced by a discount but bounded below by a minimum floor level.

concepts.name: Kirk Model
concepts.scope: An analytical approximation for pricing options on the spread between two correlated forward prices.

concepts.name: Power-Gas Correlation
concepts.scope: The statistical relationship between power and gas prices that drives spark spread option value and hedge effectiveness.

concepts.name: Implied Volatility Calibration
concepts.scope: The process of inferring market-consistent volatility parameters from observed option prices.

concepts.name: Curve Profiling
concepts.scope: The construction of granular forward price curves capturing intra-period shape from coarser market quotes.

concepts.name: Backtesting
concepts.scope: The retrospective assessment of a valuation or hedging strategy against historical market data.

concepts.name: Market Liquidity Risk
concepts.scope: The risk that insufficient trading volume impairs the ability to price, hedge or exit positions reliably.

methods: Historical analysis for daily option valuation
implied_prerequisites: Basic stochastic processes and volatility concepts

dipeng_tools.topic: Power and energy trading quantitative tools: Monte Carlo simulation, options pricing, and market data automation

concepts.name: Monte Carlo estimation
concepts.scope: Approximating expectations of functions of random variables by averaging over simulated sample paths.

concepts.name: Risk-neutral pricing
concepts.scope: Valuing derivatives as discounted expectations under the equivalent martingale measure rather than the real-world measure.

concepts.name: Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM)
concepts.scope: Continuous-time stochastic process used to model asset prices with constant drift and volatility.

concepts.name: European call option pricing
concepts.scope: Simulation-based estimation of the Black-Scholes price for a standard European call as a discounted expected payoff.

concepts.name: Asian option pricing
concepts.scope: Monte Carlo valuation of path-dependent options whose payoff depends on the average price over a period.

concepts.name: Portfolio loss probability
concepts.scope: Estimating via simulation the probability that a multi-asset portfolio value falls below a specified threshold.

concepts.name: Multivariate normal distribution
concepts.scope: Joint normal distribution over n variables characterised by a mean vector and covariance matrix.

concepts.name: Covariance and correlation matrix
concepts.scope: Symmetric positive semi-definite matrix summarising pairwise linear dependence among random variables.

concepts.name: Cholesky decomposition
concepts.scope: Factorisation of a symmetric positive-definite matrix used to generate correlated normal random vectors.

concepts.name: Correlated Brownian motions
concepts.scope: Standard Brownian motions with non-zero cross-covariance, used to drive correlated asset price processes.

concepts.name: Multivariate lognormal simulation
concepts.scope: Generating correlated lognormal random vectors by exponentiating a correlated multivariate normal draw.

concepts.name: Marginal distribution and copula-style construction
concepts.scope: Specifying only marginals and a correlation matrix and using a Gaussian mapping to construct a joint distribution.

concepts.name: Strong Law of Large Numbers (SLLN)
concepts.scope: Theoretical guarantee that the Monte Carlo sample mean converges almost surely to the true expectation.

concepts.name: Indicator function estimation
concepts.scope: Representing probabilities as expectations of binary indicator random variables for use in Monte Carlo.

concepts.name: Power market data products
concepts.scope: Baseload, peak, and hourly electricity forward products across NL, UK, DE, FR, BE markets collected for quantitative analysis.

concepts.name: Trade data query and automation
concepts.scope: Systematic retrieval and reformatting of trade records from internal systems into structured spreadsheet outputs.

concepts.name: NBP and TTF gas price data
concepts.scope: Historical spot and forward price series for UK NBP and Dutch TTF natural gas hubs used alongside power data.

concepts.name: Cubic spline interpolation
concepts.scope: Piecewise polynomial fitting used to interpolate forward curves or volatility surfaces from observed market quotes.

concepts.name: Vanilla options pricing model
concepts.scope: Spreadsheet implementation of standard call and put option valuation under Black-Scholes or related frameworks.

concepts.name: Binary/digital option valuation
concepts.scope: Pricing of options with discontinuous payoffs that pay a fixed amount if a condition is met at expiry.

methods: Indicator function Monte Carlo for probability estimation
Gaussian copula construction for marginal-only-specified dependence
implied_prerequisites: Energy market product structures (baseload, peak, hourly)

dipeng_vol_model.topic: Power and gas volatility modelling: electricity–gas spread volatility and correlation across UK, NL and DE markets

concepts.name: Baseload volatility
concepts.scope: Annualised implied or realised percentage volatility of baseload power forward prices for a given seasonal contract.

concepts.name: Peak volatility
concepts.scope: Annualised percentage volatility of peak-hour power forward prices for a given seasonal contract.

concepts.name: Gas price volatility (NBP/TTF)
concepts.scope: Annualised percentage volatility of the corresponding natural-gas forward price used as the fuel reference leg.

concepts.name: Spark-spread volatility
concepts.scope: Volatility of the differential between a power forward price and its gas-price reference, derived from the individual legs and their correlation.

concepts.name: Power–gas correlation
concepts.scope: Linear correlation coefficient between daily log-returns of a power forward and its associated gas forward over the same delivery period.

concepts.name: Seasonal contract segmentation (1SA / 2SA)
concepts.scope: Decomposition of volatility and correlation estimates by near and far seasonal forward contracts to capture term-structure effects.

concepts.name: Baseload–peak volatility differential
concepts.scope: Comparison of volatility levels between baseload and peak power contracts for the same delivery period, reflecting shape risk.

concepts.name: Forward contract tenor
concepts.scope: Classification of delivery periods (day-ahead, month-ahead, quarter-ahead, season-ahead) used to organise vol output files.

concepts.name: Volatility term structure
concepts.scope: Pattern of how volatility estimates change across successive forward maturities from day-ahead to multi-season horizons.

concepts.name: Sampling frequency in vol estimation
concepts.scope: Choice of intraday (5-minute) versus daily return intervals used to compute volatility, affecting noise and bias in estimates.

methods: Historical volatility estimation from daily log-returns
Spread volatility derivation via two-asset volatility formula
Pearson correlation estimation between power and gas return series
Seasonal and tenor stratification of volatility outputs
Cross-market comparison (UK NBP, NL TTF, DE power)

Log-return calculation and annualisation of volatility
Understanding of baseload and peak power product definitions
Familiarity with NBP, TTF gas price benchmarks

dipeng_volatility_model.topic: UK power volatility modelling for seasonal and spread contracts

concepts.name: Seasonal contract volatility
concepts.scope: Implied or realised volatility measured on forward seasonal (Summer/Winter) power contracts.

concepts.name: Spread volatility
concepts.scope: Volatility of the price spread between two related forward contracts, e.g. power vs gas.

concepts.name: Relative volatility
concepts.scope: Volatility of a contract expressed relative to a benchmark such as the day-ahead contract.

concepts.name: Time-to-maturity term structure
concepts.scope: How volatility or correlation changes as a forward contract approaches its delivery period.

concepts.name: Correlation modelling
concepts.scope: Estimation and forecasting of correlations between seasonal power contracts or between power and gas.

concepts.name: Moving-average volatility
concepts.scope: A rolling historical volatility estimate used as a smoothing and forecasting input.

concepts.name: Seasonality in volatility
concepts.scope: Systematic calendar patterns in forward contract volatility levels across Summer and Winter periods.

concepts.name: Volatility term structure forecast
concepts.scope: Out-of-sample projection of the volatility curve for a specific seasonal contract as a function of time to maturity.

concepts.name: Power-gas spread
concepts.scope: The price differential between UK baseload power and NBP gas used to decompose power volatility.

concepts.name: Volatility curve model
concepts.scope: A parametric or empirical model that maps implied or realised volatility across maturities for power contracts.

concepts.name: ATM volatility
concepts.scope: At-the-money volatility extracted from option prices or approximated from forward price data.

concepts.name: Skew
concepts.scope: The asymmetry of the implied volatility smile across strikes for power options.

concepts.name: Day-ahead (DA) volatility
concepts.scope: Short-dated spot-proxy volatility used as an anchor to derive longer-dated seasonal volatilities.

methods: Power volatility derivation from gas and spark-spread volatilities

UK power and NBP gas market structure

dipeng_wind.topic: Wind turbine hourly power output simulation

concepts.name: Wind speed time series
concepts.scope: Hub-height (115 m) wind speed observations recorded at hourly intervals for each simulated period.

concepts.name: Wind direction time series
concepts.scope: Hub-height (115 m) wind direction in degrees recorded alongside speed for each hourly interval.

concepts.name: Wind turbine power output (kW)
concepts.scope: Instantaneous active power produced by a single wind turbine generator derived from wind speed via a power curve.

concepts.name: Wind turbine energy output (kWh)
concepts.scope: Hourly energy generation equal to the average power over each one-hour period, numerically identical to kW for one-hour intervals.

concepts.name: Power curve
concepts.scope: The nonlinear relationship mapping hub-height wind speed to turbine electrical output, including cut-in, rated, and cut-out thresholds.

concepts.name: Cut-in and cut-out wind speed
concepts.scope: Lower and upper wind speed bounds outside which the turbine produces zero output, observable in the data as zero kW entries.

concepts.name: Rated power
concepts.scope: The maximum nameplate capacity of the turbine (~3 MW), reached and held constant above a certain wind speed.

concepts.name: Long-run wind resource simulation
concepts.scope: Multi-year (20-year) synthetic or reanalysis-derived hourly wind series used to characterise the statistical distribution of wind generation.

concepts.name: Capacity factor
concepts.scope: The ratio of actual energy produced to maximum possible energy over a period, derivable by aggregating the hourly output series.

concepts.name: Wind variability and intermittency
concepts.scope: The short-term and seasonal fluctuations in wind speed that cause large swings in turbine output within and across days.

concepts.name: Wind direction
concepts.scope: Meteorological bearing in degrees indicating the compass direction from which wind is blowing at each observation interval.

concepts.name: Wind speed
concepts.scope: Measured wind velocity in metres per second recorded at hourly sub-intervals for a wind generation site.

concepts.name: Wind power output
concepts.scope: Electrical power generated by a wind turbine or farm in kilowatts derived from observed wind speed at each time step.

concepts.name: Turbine capacity cap
concepts.scope: Maximum rated power output of the wind installation above which generated power is curtailed or saturated regardless of wind speed.

concepts.name: Hourly time series resolution
concepts.scope: Temporal granularity of observations recorded at 30-minute or 1-hour intervals over a multi-month period.

concepts.name: Wind power curve
concepts.scope: Nonlinear functional relationship mapping wind speed to power output, exhibiting a cubic region and a rated-power plateau.

concepts.name: Capacity constraint / rated power clipping
concepts.scope: The phenomenon whereby power output is capped at the turbine nameplate rating when wind speed exceeds the rated threshold.

concepts.name: Half-hourly settlement interval
concepts.scope: The 30-minute metering and trading period implicit in the data timestamps, relevant to GB-style electricity market settlement.

concepts.name: Intermittency and variability
concepts.scope: The irregular, weather-driven fluctuation of wind generation output that complicates scheduling and forecasting.

concepts.name: Wind turbine power output
concepts.scope: Conversion of measured wind speed into electrical power generation at hourly or sub-hourly resolution.

concepts.name: Cut-in and rated speed thresholds
concepts.scope: Wind speed boundaries that determine zero-output, partial-output, and full-rated-output operating regimes for a turbine.

concepts.name: Imbalance cost
concepts.scope: Financial penalty or settlement charge arising from deviations between forecast and actual wind generation within a balancing regime.

concepts.name: Generation forecast
concepts.scope: Predicted wind power output at turbine or portfolio level used as the basis for energy scheduling.

concepts.name: Forecast error
concepts.scope: Difference between forecast and actual generation, driving imbalance exposure for wind assets.

concepts.name: Imbalance settlement
concepts.scope: Market mechanism by which deviations from contracted positions are priced and charged to generators.

concepts.name: Onshore vs offshore wind economics
concepts.scope: Comparative cost and revenue structure distinguishing land-based from marine wind installations.

concepts.name: Portfolio aggregation of wind assets
concepts.scope: Combining individual turbine or farm outputs and forecasts to assess net imbalance at a portfolio level.

concepts.name: Sub-hourly generation data
concepts.scope: Wind production records at 15-minute or 30-minute granularity used for high-resolution settlement analysis.

concepts.name: Wind farm economics
concepts.scope: Revenue, cost, and profitability assessment for a wind generation project including imbalance charges.

methods: Wind resource assessment at hub height
Wind speed to power conversion (power curve application)
implied_prerequisites: Basic fluid mechanics and wind energy physics
Understanding of wind turbine power curves
Elementary statistics for renewable resource assessment
Basic understanding of wind turbine physics
Knowledge of electricity metering and settlement intervals

dipeng_zema_testing.topic: Programmatic access to the ZEMA energy data platform via SOAP API using Python

concepts.name: ZEMA API authentication
concepts.scope: Token-based authentication mechanism required to establish a session with the ZEMA data server.

concepts.name: SOAP web service
concepts.scope: Protocol used by the ZEMA API to expose energy data services and return structured responses.

concepts.name: Data source catalogue
concepts.scope: Enumeration of named market data providers available within the ZEMA database, such as EEX, National Grid, and Amprion.

concepts.name: Data report
concepts.scope: A named dataset within a data source representing a specific published series, such as power available capacity or generation.

concepts.name: Observations retrieval
concepts.scope: Fetching the measurable series identifiers (e.g. available capacity) associated with a specific data report.

concepts.name: Attribute values
concepts.scope: Metadata dimensions attached to a data report, including country, fuel source type, and creation timestamp, used to filter or slice time series.

concepts.name: Holiday calendar
concepts.scope: Named sets of market-specific non-trading days used to adjust or filter time series data for exchanges and jurisdictions globally.

concepts.name: Unit conversion
concepts.scope: API-supported mapping from a source energy unit (MWh) to a wide range of target units for normalising power and energy data.

concepts.name: Day-type filter
concepts.scope: Identifiers allowing time series to be restricted to specific day categories such as weekday, weekend, or named holiday sets.

concepts.name: Client profile
concepts.scope: User-level configuration objects retrievable from the ZEMA server that define saved queries or access settings.

concepts.name: Time-series date enumeration
concepts.scope: Sequential daily date labels used to index or select energy market data records within a data management platform.

concepts.name: Data platform UI parameter selection
concepts.scope: Structured label-value pair schema for defining selectable date parameters in an energy data retrieval interface.

concepts.name: SOAP web service response parsing
concepts.scope: Extraction of structured energy market data from XML SOAP envelope responses returned by a data platform API.

concepts.name: Analytic profile management
concepts.scope: Organisation of named user-defined analytic configurations covering power, gas, and weather data within a multi-user platform.

concepts.name: Data access control
concepts.scope: Classification of analytic profiles by access type (Public) and user ownership within a shared energy data environment.

concepts.name: Generation by fuel type reporting
concepts.scope: Retrieval and presentation of electricity generation data disaggregated by fuel source across multiple European markets.

concepts.name: Renewable energy forecast vs actual comparison
concepts.scope: Profile-level configuration for comparing forecast and observed solar and wind generation data at regional granularity.

concepts.name: Gas infrastructure operational data
concepts.scope: Profiles referencing pipeline and LNG terminal flow and operational metrics from gas transmission system operators.

concepts.name: ZEMA API authentication token
concepts.scope: Credential token obtained from the ZEMA server to authorise subsequent API calls.

concepts.name: Data source enumeration
concepts.scope: Retrieval of the full list of available energy data providers accessible through the ZEMA platform.

concepts.name: Data report retrieval
concepts.scope: Fetching the catalogue of data reports associated with a specific energy data source.

concepts.name: Observation retrieval
concepts.scope: Accessing individual observable fields or series available within a named data report.

concepts.name: Attribute value retrieval
concepts.scope: Querying the dimension values (e.g. country, fuel type) that filter records within a data report.

concepts.name: Holiday group catalogue
concepts.scope: A reference list of named calendar holiday schedules used to exclude non-trading days from data profiles.

concepts.name: Unit conversion lookup
concepts.scope: Retrieval of target unit options available when converting energy quantities from a specified source unit.

concepts.name: Analytic profile
concepts.scope: A saved user configuration object in ZEMA specifying data selection, analytic type, and calendar exclusion rules.

concepts.name: Day-of-week and holiday filter
concepts.scope: Predefined filter identifiers used to include or exclude specific weekdays or holiday calendars from time series.

concepts.name: SOAP web service interface
concepts.scope: The SOAPpy-based remote procedure call mechanism used to invoke ZEMA platform services from Python.

methods: SOAP API calls via Python SOAPpy library
XML/structured markup for UI parameter binding

Familiarity with energy market data concepts
Basic understanding of energy market data systems
Basic understanding of XML and SOAP protocols

Knowledge of power and gas market data types
Understanding of calendar conventions in energy markets

dipeng_battery.topic: Battery energy storage: technology, valuation, grid services and testing

concepts.name: Battery energy storage system (BESS)
concepts.scope: Modular electrochemical storage combining cells, power conversion and control to import/export power from a grid connection.

concepts.name: Power Conversion System (PCS) / inverter
concepts.scope: Power-electronic device that converts DC energy stored in batteries to AC power suitable for grid injection.

concepts.name: State of charge (SoC)
concepts.scope: Instantaneous energy level of a battery expressed as a fraction of its total capacity, governing available discharge duration.

concepts.name: Round-trip efficiency (RTE)
concepts.scope: Ratio of energy delivered on discharge to energy consumed on charge, determining net energy loss per storage cycle.

concepts.name: Cycle life
concepts.scope: Total number of full charge/discharge cycles a battery can sustain before capacity degrades to an end-of-life threshold.

concepts.name: Storage duration
concepts.scope: Hours over which a fully charged storage device can discharge at rated power, linking energy capacity to power rating.

concepts.name: Peak shaving
concepts.scope: Primary network application where storage discharges during demand peaks to reduce load on a constrained circuit below its security rating.

concepts.name: N-1 network security
concepts.scope: Planning criterion requiring the network to remain within rated limits following loss of any single circuit or transformer.

concepts.name: Firm Frequency Response (FFR)
concepts.scope: Contracted, continuously proportional modulation of active power in response to real-time frequency deviation from 50 Hz.

concepts.name: Dynamic frequency response
concepts.scope: Continuous, proportional MW adjustment delivered within seconds of a frequency deviation to manage second-by-second system balance.

concepts.name: Static (non-dynamic) frequency response
concepts.scope: Discrete full-power step response triggered automatically when system frequency crosses a pre-agreed threshold.

concepts.name: Frequency Control by Demand Management (FCDM)
concepts.scope: Demand interruption service that activates automatically via under-frequency relay to arrest low-frequency events.

concepts.name: Demand Side Response (DSR)
concepts.scope: Deliberate modification of an end-user's metered consumption in response to an external signal to provide grid balancing services.

concepts.name: Virtual power plant (VPP)
concepts.scope: Aggregation of distributed storage or demand assets controlled in coordination to appear as a single dispatchable resource to the system operator.

concepts.name: Short-Term Operating Reserve (STOR)
concepts.scope: Contracted service providing a full-power export from storage triggered by the system operator to cover transmission outages.

concepts.name: Energy arbitrage (time shifting)
concepts.scope: Revenue strategy of charging storage during low-price periods and discharging during high-price periods to capture price spreads.

concepts.name: Ancillary services revenue
concepts.scope: Payments received for providing frequency regulation, reserve or other balancing services that complement energy arbitrage income.

concepts.name: Capex break-even ($/kW or $/kWh)
concepts.scope: Maximum installed cost at which a storage project achieves zero NPV given projected revenues from energy and ancillary services.

concepts.name: NPV / IRR project valuation
concepts.scope: Discounted cash-flow metrics used to assess whether projected storage revenues justify capital expenditure under given market conditions.

concepts.name: On-peak / off-peak price spread
concepts.scope: Difference between high-demand and low-demand wholesale electricity prices that determines the theoretical arbitrage value available to storage.

concepts.name: Capacity payment
concepts.scope: Fixed periodic payment received by a storage asset for being available to generate, equivalent to a boost in effective energy price.

concepts.name: Levelized cost of storage ($/kWh/cycle)
concepts.scope: All-in annualised cost of providing one kWh of discharged energy over the asset lifetime, used to compare storage technologies.

concepts.name: Sodium-sulphur (NaS) battery
concepts.scope: High-temperature electrochemical storage technology characterised by long duration (≈7.5 h), moderate efficiency and high capital cost per kW.

concepts.name: Lithium-ion battery
concepts.scope: Electrochemical storage technology offering high efficiency and short duration (≈1 h) with capital costs stated per kWh of usable capacity.

concepts.name: Flow battery (zinc-bromide)
concepts.scope: Electrochemical storage technology with energy stored in liquid electrolytes, offering medium duration and lower round-trip efficiency than lithium-ion.

concepts.name: Forecasting, Optimisation and Scheduling System (FOSS)
concepts.scope: Software layer that forecasts network demand, schedules commercial services and communicates a suggested dispatch plan to the on-site battery manager.

concepts.name: Battery Energy Storage System Manager (BESSM)
concepts.scope: On-site control system that executes scheduled services, responds to real-time network conditions and manages state of charge across battery arrays.

concepts.name: Enhanced Frequency Control Capability (EFCC)
concepts.scope: NIC-funded innovation project testing battery storage paired with solar PV to provide enhanced frequency response to the GB transmission system.

concepts.name: Network Innovation Competition (NIC) funding
concepts.scope: Ofgem-administered mechanism providing ring-fenced consumer funding for electricity network innovation projects subject to cost-benefit scrutiny.

concepts.name: Cost-benefit analysis (CBA) for storage innovation
concepts.scope: Quantitative appraisal monetising learning benefits and consumer costs of a funded storage trial to justify public expenditure.

concepts.name: Solar PV–battery hybrid
concepts.scope: Co-located pairing of photovoltaic generation with battery storage to smooth ramp events and provide frequency response services.

concepts.name: Proportionality of frequency response
concepts.scope: Requirement that a provider's MW output change be linearly proportional to the deviation of system frequency from 50 Hz.

concepts.name: Response delay (K)
concepts.scope: End-to-end time from frequency deviation detection to full MW delivery by the service provider, typically no more than two seconds.

concepts.name: Frequency response testing protocol
concepts.scope: Structured sequence of injected frequency signals and hold periods used to demonstrate speed, proportionality and sustainability of a provider's response.

concepts.name: Tolling
concepts.scope: Fixed daily import/export schedule contracted at full rated power over a defined period, providing predictable utilisation of storage capacity.

concepts.name: Market structure sensitivity (storage economics)
concepts.scope: Variation in storage project break-even capex across ISO regions driven by differences in energy spreads, ancillary service rates and capacity mechanisms.

concepts.name: Static Frequency Response
concepts.scope: A grid service triggered at a defined frequency threshold and sustained continuously for a bilaterally agreed period regardless of subsequent frequency movements.

concepts.name: Enhanced Frequency Response (EFR)
concepts.scope: A fast-acting GB ancillary service providing synthetic inertia or pre-fault frequency control within a sub-second timescale, procured via competitive tender.

concepts.name: System Inertia
concepts.scope: The resistance of grid frequency to rapid change, historically provided by synchronous thermal plant and diminishing as non-synchronous renewables displace conventional generation.

concepts.name: Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF)
concepts.scope: The speed at which system frequency deviates following a generation-demand imbalance event, which increases as system inertia falls.

concepts.name: State of Charge (SoC) Management
concepts.scope: The operational practice of maintaining battery energy levels within bounds to ensure continuous availability of frequency response services.

concepts.name: Frequency Deadband
concepts.scope: A frequency range around 50 Hz within which no mandatory response is triggered, used to facilitate storage state-of-charge management.

concepts.name: Delivery Saturation
concepts.scope: The requirement for full contracted MW delivery to be achieved within a specified frequency deviation range, typically ±0.2–0.3 Hz from nominal.

concepts.name: Performance Monitoring and Underperformance Deduction
concepts.scope: A contractual mechanism calculating provider shortfall as actual versus contracted response, deducting fees across the affected settlement periods.

concepts.name: Revenue Layering
concepts.scope: The stacking of multiple income streams (EFR, FFR, TRIAD, capacity market, arbitrage) across a single battery asset to improve project economics.

concepts.name: TRIAD Avoidance
concepts.scope: An embedded benefit accruing to demand-side or storage assets that reduce consumption during the three half-hours of highest system demand, lowering TNUoS charges.

concepts.name: Capacity Market
concepts.scope: A GB mechanism awarding multi-year payments to assets that commit to deliver capacity during stress events, providing an additional revenue stream for storage.

concepts.name: Aggregation Growth Model
concepts.scope: A service provision structure where a portfolio MW level grows over time as additional assets join, requiring agreed re-testing protocols with the TSO.

concepts.name: Monitoring and Control System (MCS)
concepts.scope: A wide-area technology platform using phasor measurement units to detect regional frequency and RoCoF and dispatch proportionate fast response from diverse resources.

concepts.name: Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU)
concepts.scope: A device measuring voltage and current phasors at high temporal resolution to provide accurate regional frequency and RoCoF data for grid control.

concepts.name: Synthetic Inertia
concepts.scope: Emulated inertial response provided by power-electronic-interfaced resources replicating the frequency-stabilising behaviour of synchronous rotating machines.

concepts.name: Battery Utilisation Rate
concepts.scope: The proportion of time or energy throughput for which a battery asset is actively delivering a contracted frequency response service.

concepts.name: Connection Approach and Embedded Benefits
concepts.scope: The choice between transmission and distribution connection, determining applicable network charges (TNUoS, GDUoS, BSUoS) and access to benefits such as TRIAD reduction.

concepts.name: Battery Storage CAPEX and Economics
concepts.scope: The capital expenditure profile and sensitivity analysis underpinning the business case for grid-scale battery projects, incorporating technology cost forecasts.

concepts.name: Technical Readiness Level (TRL)
concepts.scope: A European Commission scale used by National Grid to screen EFR tender submissions for deployment readiness, requiring TRL 7 or above.

concepts.name: Tender Assessment and Value Ratio
concepts.scope: The process of evaluating EFR bids against the avoided cost of alternative frequency response procurement, using a stated 2:1 value ratio versus existing PSH services at certain periods.

concepts.name: Frequency Response
concepts.scope: Active power adjustment by generators or loads to arrest and correct frequency deviations after a system event.

concepts.name: Largest Infeed Loss
concepts.scope: The dimensioning contingency for frequency response procurement, representing the sudden loss of the largest single generation or demand source on the system.

concepts.name: Non-synchronous Generation
concepts.scope: Generation connected via power electronics (wind, solar PV, HVDC) that contributes no natural inertia to the AC system.

concepts.name: Rapid Response
concepts.scope: Frequency response activated within milliseconds of a disturbance, enabling a smaller volume of resource to replace larger volumes of slower conventional response.

concepts.name: Wide-Area Measurement (PMU/Phasor)
concepts.scope: Synchronised phasor measurements across geographically dispersed grid nodes used to detect disturbances and measure frequency and RoCoF with high resolution.

concepts.name: Demand-Side Response (DSR)
concepts.scope: Voluntary or automated curtailment or shifting of industrial and commercial electricity consumption to provide grid balancing services.

concepts.name: Battery Energy Storage
concepts.scope: Grid-connected battery systems capable of injecting or absorbing power within milliseconds to provide frequency regulation and virtual inertia.

concepts.name: Virtual Inertia
concepts.scope: Synthetic inertia emulated by power-electronic-interfaced storage or generation to slow RoCoF in the absence of synchronous rotating mass.

concepts.name: df/dt Control vs Absolute Frequency Control
concepts.scope: Two trigger philosophies for response dispatch: reacting to the rate of frequency change versus reacting to a threshold frequency level.

concepts.name: Balancing Services Use of System (BSUoS)
concepts.scope: A daily flat tariff charged to generators and suppliers that recovers National Grid's real-time balancing costs including frequency control.

concepts.name: Must-Run Constraints
concepts.scope: Obligations to keep synchronous thermal units online to maintain inertia levels, incurring out-of-merit dispatch costs.

concepts.name: Response Scheduling
concepts.scope: Forward planning of the mix and volume of frequency response services procured to balance cost, carbon and security requirements.

concepts.name: Low Part Load Operation
concepts.scope: Running thermal generators at output levels well below rated capacity to hold headroom for frequency response, at a thermal efficiency and cost penalty.

concepts.name: PV Power Plant Grid Support
concepts.scope: Operating photovoltaic plants below maximum power point or using inverter reserves to deliver reactive power and fast active-power frequency response.

concepts.name: RoCoF Relay Settings
concepts.scope: Protection relay thresholds that trip embedded generators when RoCoF exceeds a set value, creating cascading disconnection risk under low-inertia conditions.

concepts.name: Cost-Benefit Analysis of Frequency Response Options
concepts.scope: Quantitative comparison of annual costs of conventional frequency management alternatives against the EFCC approach to justify innovation investment.

concepts.name: Wide-area monitoring and control
concepts.scope: Use of geographically distributed measurements to coordinate control actions across an entire transmission system.

concepts.name: Event detection algorithm
concepts.scope: Software logic that distinguishes genuine frequency events from disturbances to trigger appropriate control responses.

concepts.name: Resource allocation algorithm
concepts.scope: An optimisation routine that selects and schedules available response providers based on capability and cost.

concepts.name: Technology Readiness Level (TRL)
concepts.scope: A scale used to assess the maturity of a technology from concept through to full commercial deployment.

concepts.name: Balancing Services
concepts.scope: Ancillary services procured by the system operator to maintain real-time supply-demand balance, including frequency response products.

concepts.name: Balancing and Settlement Code (BSC)
concepts.scope: The regulatory code governing electricity balancing and settlement arrangements in Great Britain.

concepts.name: Wind curtailment avoidance
concepts.scope: Reduction in the volume of wind generation that must be constrained off during low-demand periods through better frequency management.

concepts.name: Cost-benefit analysis (CBA)
concepts.scope: Quantitative comparison of project costs against projected financial and carbon savings from improved frequency response procurement.

methods: Sensitivity / tornado analysis on storage project economics
Frequency response testing schedules (dynamic and static)
Demand forecasting for network security scheduling
Frequency response compliance testing (static and dynamic test sequences)
Cost-benefit analysis of frequency response under future inertia scenarios
Sensitivity analysis on EFR payment and battery utilisation
Phasor measurement and wide-area frequency monitoring
Second-by-second frequency data analysis for SoC management
Competitive tender assessment against avoided-cost baseline
Real-time wide-area disturbance detection and classification
Technology trial and demonstration on live transmission system
Response capability characterisation across multiple technology types
Carbon savings estimation under Gone Green and Slow Progression scenarios
Representative network model development and validation

dipeng_news.topic: Energy trading personnel movements and commodity book divestitures

concepts.scope: Trading of derivative instruments referencing energy commodities such as oil, gas, and power.

dipeng_presentation.topic: China Emissions Trading Scheme pilot markets and exchange registration

concepts.name: Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) pilot programme
concepts.scope: Regional cap-and-trade schemes selected by NDRC across seven Chinese cities/provinces as precursors to a national market.

concepts.name: Chinese Certified Emission Reduction (CCER)
concepts.scope: Domestic project-based offset mechanism generating credits eligible for compliance use within China's pilot ETS schemes.

concepts.name: Price controls on exchange trading
concepts.scope: Regulatory limits on permissible trade prices that restrict the formation of forward or large-volume transactions on Chinese emissions exchanges.

concepts.name: Central Counterparty (CCP)
concepts.scope: An entity that interposes itself between buyer and seller to guarantee trade settlement and enable anonymous execution with margining.

concepts.name: Exchange membership and trading access
concepts.scope: Structural constraints on the number of login credentials per member that limit simultaneous trading and compliance monitoring.

concepts.name: Know Your Customer (KYC) in anonymous exchange markets
concepts.scope: The challenge of satisfying counterparty identification requirements when exchange spot trades are executed anonymously pre- and post-deal.

concepts.name: OTC versus exchange spot trading
concepts.scope: Distinction between bilaterally negotiated over-the-counter transactions and exchange-executed spot trades in emissions allowances.

concepts.name: Forward trading with cleared CCP settlement
concepts.scope: Exchange-listed forward contracts on emissions allowances novated and margined through a central clearing house.

concepts.name: Minimum volume commitment
concepts.scope: A negotiated trading obligation whereby a participant guarantees a threshold annual volume in exchange for reduced exchange fees.

Negotiation of bespoke trading rules and fee structures

dipeng_valuation_reports.topic: Power plant and spread option valuation across European electricity markets

concepts.name: Intrinsic value
concepts.scope: The deterministic value of a power plant or spread option derived from the current hourly shaped price forward curve.

concepts.name: Extrinsic (time) value
concepts.scope: The component of plant or option value beyond intrinsic, arising from price volatility and the optionality of future dispatch decisions.

concepts.name: Clean dark spread
concepts.scope: The margin of a coal-fired plant after deducting coal fuel costs and carbon allowance costs from the power price.

concepts.name: Clean spark spread
concepts.scope: The margin of a gas-fired plant after deducting gas fuel costs and carbon allowance costs from the power price.

concepts.name: Spread option strip
concepts.scope: A series of hourly European-style options on the clean spark or dark spread, representing the upper bound of plant optionality with no start costs.

concepts.name: Real plant product
concepts.scope: A power station model that incorporates start costs, part-load efficiency penalties, and variable operating costs to reflect actual dispatch constraints.

concepts.name: Hourly shaped price forward curve
concepts.scope: A forward curve disaggregated to hourly resolution to capture intraday price seasonality for plant dispatch valuation.

concepts.name: UK Carbon Price Floor
concepts.scope: A UK-specific carbon tax that supplements EU ETS allowance prices, effectively raising the carbon cost faced by UK generators.

concepts.name: Delta hedging
concepts.scope: A dynamic replication strategy that locks in a portion of extrinsic option value by continuously hedging the price sensitivity of the plant position.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo simulation for dispatch optimisation
concepts.scope: Stochastic simulation of commodity prices used to estimate expected plant value by averaging payoffs over many price paths.

concepts.name: Least-squares Monte Carlo (LSMC)
concepts.scope: A regression-based dynamic programming method applied within Monte Carlo simulation to determine the optimal hourly dispatch strategy.

concepts.name: Plant efficiency
concepts.scope: The heat rate or conversion ratio linking fuel input to power output, which determines the fuel cost per MWh generated.

concepts.name: Part-load operation
concepts.scope: Running a plant at reduced capacity with a lower efficiency to avoid incurring start costs when margins are thin.

concepts.name: Start cost
concepts.scope: A fixed cost incurred each time a power plant is brought from offline to generating, penalising frequent cycling in dispatch optimisation.

concepts.name: Historical calibration of volatility and correlation
concepts.scope: Estimating stochastic model parameters from observed market price data over a defined lookback window for use in simulation.

methods: Intrinsic valuation using hourly price forward curves
Historical calibration of volatility and correlation parameters
implied_prerequisites: EU ETS and carbon pricing mechanisms
